details_text: VIT Bhopal University will host Health Hackathon 3.0 on 28 and 29 January 2027. A pre-event workshop will take place on 27 January 2027. VIT Bhopal is collaborating with the Whiting School of Engineering at Johns Hopkins University for this event. Its full title is “Health Hackathon 3.0: Global Health Access Innovation Challenge – Next Generation.” New Ideas for Better Healthcare The event has a clear aim: it seeks innovative ideas that can improve healthcare accessibility for more people, reduce costs, and enhance overall efficiency. Participants are invited to propose actionable solutions to real-world healthcare challenges. Key focus areas for submissions include: Low-cost tools and technologies for healthcare delivery. New ways and platforms to support mental health. Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare solutions. Tools leveraging health data analytics to identify and predict health risks. A Chance to Share and Build Ideas Health Hackathon 3.0 invites innovators, students, and researchers to present their concepts and refine them further. The emphasis is on practical, high-impact solutions designed to reach underserved communities and individuals facing healthcare access barriers. Event Overview & Key Dates • Pre-Event Workshop: 27 January 2027 • Main Hackathon: 28 & 29 January 2027 • Venue: VIT Bhopal University, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh • Total Prize Pool: ₹2 Lakh Registration & Submission Registration is now open. Interested teams and individuals must submit their project proposals by 31 October 2026 . To learn more, view participation guidelines, and complete registration, please visit the official Health Hackathon 3.0 event website

title: DoomForge
description: About DOOMFORGE DOOMFORGE is a two-round business and engineering hackathon that challenges participants to combine strategic thinking, market analysis, and practical software engineering. The competition is designed to…
details_text: About DOOMFORGE DOOMFORGE is a two-round business and engineering hackathon that challenges participants to combine strategic thinking, market analysis, and practical software engineering. The competition is designed to take participants beyond conventional coding challenges. It begins with identifying real-world business problems and market opportunities, followed by hands-on engineering challenges involving existing codebases and open-source development. Participants will have the opportunity to demonstrate their analytical thinking, technical expertise, creativity, and ability to build practical solutions. Eligibility and Team Formation Open to college students. Team size: 1 - 3 members. Inter-college teams are allowed. Participants from different academic specialisations are welcome to collaborate. Each participant can be part of only one team. All team members must complete the registration process. Competition Structure Round 1: Market Analysis Duration: 4 December – 6 December 2026 Round 1 focuses on business strategy, market research, and problem identification. Participants will be presented with a business-oriented problem or scenario. They must analyse the problem, understand the market landscape, identify opportunities, and propose a feasible solution. What participants need to cover: Problem identification and understanding. Target audience and market analysis. Competitor research and existing solutions. Identification of market gaps and opportunities. Proposed solution, its feasibility, and potential impact. Submission Format: Teams must submit a one-minute video explaining their market analysis, identified opportunity, and proposed solution through Unstop. Evaluation Criteria: Depth of market research. Understanding of the problem. Originality and innovation. Feasibility of the proposed solution. Clarity and effectiveness of presentation. Based on their submissions, selected teams will qualify for the second round. Round 2: Engineering Arena – Open-Source Development The second round is a hands-on engineering challenge in which shortlisted teams will work on one of four dedicated GitHub repositories. Each repository represents a distinct engineering track with its own technical problem space. Participants will be expected to understand the existing codebase, identify areas for improvement, and implement meaningful technical contributions. Potential engineering challenges include: Developing new features and functionalities. Identifying and fixing bugs. Improving application performance and scalability. Implementing security enhancements. Writing automated tests and improving test coverage. Integrating AI/ML-based capabilities. Improving code quality, maintainability, and documentation. Submission Format: All development contributions must be submitted through GitHub Pull Requests (PRs) to the respective repositories. Evaluation Criteria: Functional correctness and completeness. Code quality and maintainability. Technical implementation. Security and reliability. Testing and validation. Innovation and practical impact. Engineering Tracks DOOMFORGE features four specialised engineering tracks, each backed by a dedicated GitHub repository. Participants will work on the repository and technical challenge specified by the organising team. Further details regarding the repositories, technical requirements, and challenges will be communicated to qualified participants. Rules and Regulations Teams must consist of a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3 members. Inter-college participation is permitted. Each participant may register as part of only one team. Round 1 submissions must be submitted within the specified deadline, from 4 December to 6 December 2026. Round 1 submissions must follow the prescribed one-minute video format. title: Queryquest: SQL Problem-Solving Challenge

description: QueryQuest is a technical competition organised by HackerRank Campus Crew, NIE Mysuru , designed to test participants' SQL knowledge, database concepts and problem-solving abilities. The challenge provides an…
details_text: QueryQuest is a technical competition organised by HackerRank Campus Crew, NIE Mysuru , designed to test participants' SQL knowledge, database concepts and problem-solving abilities. The challenge provides an opportunity for students to demonstrate their understanding of SQL through practical coding problems and multiple-choice questions across different difficulty levels. Competition Format The competition will consist of 10 questions to be completed within a total time limit of 100 minutes . The question distribution will be: SQL Basic – 4 Questions SQL Intermediate – 3 Questions SQL Advanced – 1 Question SQL Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) – 2 Questions Rules and Guidelines The competition will be conducted online through the HackerRank platform. Participants must complete all questions within the allotted 100 minutes. Participants must use their own HackerRank accounts to access the challenge. All submitted SQL solutions must satisfy the given problem requirements and test cases. Participants must not share solutions, collaborate with other participants or engage in any unfair practices during the competition. The use of external assistance or AI tools during the competition is not permitted. Participants must ensure a stable internet connection throughout the challenge. Tie-breaker: If two or more participants achieve the same score, the participant who completes the assessment in the shortest time will be ranked higher. For example, if two participants achieve the same score, but Participant 1 finishes at 10:00 AM and Participant 2 finishes at 11:00 AM, Participant 1 will be ranked higher. The organisers' decision regarding the results and rewards will be final. Eligibility Open to college students interested in SQL, databases and problem-solving. Participants from all engineering branches and academic years are welcome. Basic knowledge of SQL is recommended. Rewards and Recognition Winner HackerRank Infinity Plan AI Tool Credits HackerRank Mock Interview Credits Certificate of Achievement Runner-up AI Tool Credits HackerRank Mock Interview Credits Certificate of Achievement All Participants HackerRank Mock Interview Credits Participation Certificate Evaluation Process Participants will be evaluated based on the correctness of their submitted solutions and their performance in the competition. The final rankings will be determined based on the competition results.

details_text: Innovate. Build. Disrupt.: SINGULARITY is a premier inter-college hybrid hackathon organized by BLITZ, the Computer Science Society of Keshav Mahavidyalaya, University of Delhi. Web3: Building decentralized architectures, smart contracts, and blockchain-powered innovations. AR/VR & Immersive Experiences: Architecting virtual spaces and developing next-generation spatial computing interfaces. Open Innovation: Bring your own unique problem statement and develop a creative, technology-driven solution. details_text: All You Need to Know About AGENTIC X 2.0 – AI & Robotics Hackathon | Future Tech Summit ’26 AGENTIC X 2.0 is an AI & Robotics Hackathon held as part of Future Tech Summit ’26, organized by the AI Research Centre (AIRC), Woxsen University, in collaboration with Gentricks and TruScholar. The hackathon brings together innovators, developers, students, and technology enthusiasts to build creative solutions to real-world challenges through Artificial Intelligence, Agentic AI, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems. Hackathon Tracks Track 1 – Software: Agentic AI Theme: Autonomous Intelligence for the Digital World Problem Statement: Autonomous AI Agents for Intelligent Real-World Decision-Making Participants can develop innovative software solutions using AI agents, multi-agent systems, reasoning, planning, large language models (LLMs), intelligent copilots, and workflow automation. Track 2 – Hardware: Robotics & Autonomous Systems Theme: Intelligent Machines for the Physical World Problem Statement: Intelligent Autonomous Machines for Real-World Physical Challenges Participants can explore robotics, autonomous systems, embedded AI, sensors, computer vision, the Internet of Things (IoT), control systems, and intelligent machines. Submission guidelines: One submission per team, for one track only PPT only, maximum 10 slides Clearly state the problem, proposed solution, technology stack, feasibility and technical approach, potential impact, and current stage — idea-only, prototype in progress, or working prototype For Track 2, idea-only entries are accepted in Round 1. A working prototype is not mandatory in Round 1, but if you have one, include photos, a short demo video link, or test results. Submissions must be original work by the team. Submissions will be evaluated based on: Innovation and originality Problem relevance Feasibility and technical approach Potential impact Quality of the proposed solution Shortlisted teams will qualify for Round 2. Round 2 – Final Build & Demo Shortlisted teams will advance to the in-person final round at Woxsen University, Hyderabad. Participants will develop or refine their solutions and present their final build or demonstration to the judges. The full Round 2 schedule and participation details will be shared directly with shortlisted teams. Hardware teams should bring their prototype and components. If you need power, workspace, or internet support for your demo, inform the organizers in advance after shortlisting. Internship Opportunities Internship Opportunities for Hackathon Winners! Winning teams will be considered for internship opportunities with startups and AI research centres, providing a chance to gain practical experience, showcase their technical skills, and explore opportunities within the startup ecosystem. Exclusive Benefit for Hackathon Participants Free Access to All Technical Talks at Future Tech Summit ’26! Participants who register for AGENTIC X 2.0 will receive free access to all technical talks at Future Tech Summit ’26, giving them the opportunity to learn from industry experts and explore emerging technologies. This benefit covers technical talks only. Eligibility The hackathon welcomes students, freshers, professionals, and technology enthusiasts interested in AI, robotics, and emerging technologies. Team size: 1–4 members per team (a team leader plus up to 3 members). description: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is a 36-hour offline hackathon in Goa designed for students to turn their ideas into working prototypes. It offers a collaborative space to experiment with AI, web development, and emerging technologies while learning from experienced builders.
eligibility: Students, aspiring developers, designers, AI builders, and technology enthusiasts.
requirements: Technical curiosity, a willingness to collaborate, and physical attendance in Goa.
details_text: About GOA BUILDATHON ’27: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is a 36-hour offline hackathon planned for January 2027 in Goa, India. It aims to bring together developers, designers, AI enthusiasts, problem-solvers and innovators from colleges and communities to turn ideas into working solutions. This is where ideas move beyond discussions and become prototypes. Whether you're exploring AI agents, developing web applications, automating everyday workflows or experimenting with emerging technologies, GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is designed to give you the space to build, collaborate and challenge yourself. Our vision is to create an environment where students can experiment with new technologies, solve meaningful problems, learn from experienced builders and connect with people who share the same passion for creating. Not just another hackathon. A place to turn ideas into reality. What To Expect: 36 hours of offline building in Goa Collaboration with developers, designers and innovators Hands-on experimentation with AI, AI agents and automation Web development, software engineering and emerging technology Teamwork, rapid prototyping and practical problem-solving Opportunities to connect with mentors, judges and technology communities Project showcases and opportunities to present your ideas Community partnerships and potential sponsor-led challenges An environment focused on learning, creativity and building real solutions Who Can Participate?: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 welcomes students, aspiring developers, designers, AI builders and technology enthusiasts who want to learn by building. Whether you're an experienced hackathon participant or attending your first hackathon, the focus is on curiosity, collaboration and the willingness to create something meaningful. Bring your skills, find teammates, explore unfamiliar technologies and turn your ideas into something people can experience. What Can You Build?: We encourage projects across a range of technology areas, including: Artificial Intelligence & AI Agents: Build intelligent assistants, agentic workflows and practical AI-powered applications. Web Development: Create websites, platforms and full-stack applications that address real problems. Automation: Develop tools that reduce repetitive work and improve everyday processes. Data Science & Analytics: Turn data into insights, useful tools and better decisions. Software & Developer Tools: Build products that improve workflows, productivity and collaboration. Electronics & Emerging Technology: Explore innovative solutions that connect software with the physical world. The goal is not simply to present an idea, but to make meaningful progress towards a working solution within the hackathon. Why Goa?: Goa offers a distinctive setting for bringing people together to learn, collaborate and create. GOA BUILDATHON ’27 aims to combine the energy of a technology-building event with a community-driven experience where new connections and ideas can grow. We want participants to leave with more than a project: new skills, valuable connections, practical experience and the confidence to keep building. Event Details: Event: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 Format: 36-hour offline hackathon Location: Goa, India Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/goabuildathon27/ Website: https://goabuilds.com/ Contact: hello@goabuilds.com The event dates, venue, registration details, prize pool and other final arrangements will be announced through official channels once confirmed. Be Part Of The Build: We're bringing together people who don't just want to talk about ideas — they want to build them. If you have an idea worth exploring, a problem worth solving or simply the curiosity to create something new, GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is your opportunity to get started. Build > Collaborate > Create real impact Let's build something that matters.

details_text: About the Event The AI Hackathon is an event organised by Infinity - The Tech Society of Sri Guru Gobind Singh College of Commerce, University of Delhi , as part of TechTonics 2026. Teams of four will compete to build a website based on a problem statement revealed at the venue. Participants will have 90 minutes (1.5 hours) to brainstorm, design, develop, and finalise their websites using AI tools. The event aims to promote innovation, problem-solving, teamwork, and the practical application of AI in web development. Eligibility Each team must consist of maximum 4 members . Registration must be completed as a team through Unstop. All team members must be registered before the competition begins. Teams must develop their websites within the allotted 90 minutes. Participants must bring their own laptops and ensure they are ready for use. Teams must submit their final website before the deadline. Plagiarism, copying another team's work, or submitting someone else's work as original may result in disqualification. Participants must follow all instructions given by the organisers. The judges' decision will be final. Functionality: Working features and usability of the website. Relevance: Effectiveness in addressing the given problem statement. Internet availability will depend on venue facilities; participants should plan accordingly. Participants must report to the venue at the time communicated by the organisers. details_text: MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution. A Multidisciplinary Innovation Hackathon About the Opportunity MADLAB is a high-energy, multidisciplinary hackathon designed for individuals who dare to think differently, communicate confidently, build creatively, and execute ideas into practical solutions. The competition brings together software developers, marketing enthusiasts, sales strategists, business students, designers, and aspiring entrepreneurs to solve challenges through innovation, teamwork, and strategic thinking. This is not just a coding competition. Participants will be evaluated on their creativity, technical and practical skills, communication, problem-solving, marketing strategies, sales approach, and ability to present and execute ideas. Eligibility Criteria Open to college students and aspiring professionals with an interest in technology, business, marketing, sales, design, or entrepreneurship. Participants from all academic streams and specializations are welcome. Students from different colleges can form a team together (inter-college participation is allowed). Participants from different specializations can collaborate in the same team (inter-specialization participation is encouraged). No advanced coding experience is mandatory. Creativity, communication, business thinking, and execution matter just as much as technical skills. Participants must provide accurate registration details and follow the event organizers' instructions. Team Formation Participants may register individually or in teams of 2–5 members. Teams may include developers, marketers, sales representatives, designers, presenters, and business strategists. Each team should distribute responsibilities effectively and ensure that every member contributes. Each team must nominate one member as its primary point of contact. Team changes after registration require approval from the organizers. Competition Format and Rounds Round 1: The Spark — Problem-Solving and Ideation (30 minutes) Teams receive a problem statement and identify the problem, target audience, and potential solution. They must demonstrate original thinking, practical reasoning, and a clear understanding of the challenge. Round 2: The Build Lab — Creation and Strategy (90 minutes) Teams develop a working prototype, business concept, marketing campaign, sales strategy, or another relevant solution according to the assigned challenge. Developers can build prototypes, marketers can design campaigns, and sales-oriented participants can develop pitches and customer acquisition strategies. Round 3: The Pitch Arena — Presentation and Communication (5–7 minutes per team) Each team presents its solution to the judges, explaining the problem, proposed solution, target audience, implementation strategy, and expected impact. Teams must communicate their ideas clearly and confidently. Round 4: The Crossfire — Judges' Q&A (3–5 minutes per team) Judges question teams about their decisions, originality, feasibility, technical implementation, marketing approach, sales strategy, and scalability. Participants must demonstrate ownership of their work and respond professionally. Total estimated competition duration: 2.5–4 hours, depending on the number of teams and event scheduling. Problem Statements Participants will receive one assigned problem statement or challenge from the organizers. Challenges may cover the following areas: Technology and Development: Build a prototype, tool, website, application, or automation that solves a real-world problem. Marketing and Creativity: Develop a creative marketing campaign, brand strategy, social media concept, or customer engagement plan. Sales and Business Growth: Create a sales pitch, customer acquisition strategy, conversion plan, or business growth model. Communication and Innovation: Present an original idea, demonstrate persuasive communication, and turn a concept into an actionable solution. details_text: Overview: ELUCode is a fast-paced 2-hour competitive coding contest by EduLinkUp designed to challenge your problem-solving ability, algorithmic thinking, and coding speed. The contest brings together students and developers from across the community to compete on a set of carefully curated problems ranging from logical puzzles to algorithmic challenges. Participants will face multiple problems of varying difficulty levels, testing their understanding of data structures, algorithms, logic building, and efficient coding practices. Whether you are a beginner exploring competitive programming or an experienced coder looking to sharpen your skills, ELUCode provides a platform to learn, compete, and showcase your abilities. Top performers will be recognised through special achievement badges and certificates within the EduLinkUp ecosystem. Scoring: Each challenge carries a predefined score, based on its difficulty level. A participant’s score for a challenge depends on the number of test cases successfully passed by their submission. Submissions are automatically evaluated against hidden and visible test cases to ensure correctness and efficiency. The overall leaderboard is determined by the total score obtained across all challenges. If two or more participants achieve the same score, the tie will be broken based on the sum of time of the first correct solution for all the problems. The participant who reaches the score earlier will rank higher.

description: About: An engaging mix of algorithmic strategy, autonomous decision-making, and competitive resource management, this event puts participants in command of programmable rover fleets competing for dominance on an…
details_text: About: An engaging mix of algorithmic strategy, autonomous decision-making, and competitive resource management, this event puts participants in command of programmable rover fleets competing for dominance on an unpredictable battlefield. Participants must design intelligent controllers to explore unfamiliar terrain, gather resources, defend their territory, and outmanoeuvre rival teams. With mechanics ranging from hidden hazards and tactical combat to resource-driven upgrades and enemy vault raids, every decision can shift the balance of the game. The event tests participants' programming skills, strategic thinking, adaptability, and ability to make optimal decisions under uncertainty. The event will unfold in two stages . Prelims (Online): Format: Submission-based programming round hosted on Unstop. Description: Participants develop and submit autonomous rover controllers to compete in a head-to-head, turn-based strategy game. The round challenges participants to explore a simulated environment, gather resources, and outmanoeuvre their opponents through intelligent decision-making. Algorithmic thinking, tactical planning, and efficient resource management are key to advancing. Finals (Offline): Format: On-site interactive competition conducted at IIT Madras. Description: Shortlisted participants compete in a live, turn-based rover strategy game featuring a free-for-all format. Participants must program their rovers to explore the map, mine resources, raid enemy vaults, engage in combat, and manage upgrades to maximise their score. The finals also introduce a dynamic in-game market, adding an economic dimension where participants must make strategic decisions about resource allocation, purchases, and upgrades. Adaptability, tactical thinking, and intelligent resource management will be crucial to securing victory. Date: To be held during Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras. The event follows a team-based format, with 2–3 participants per team, encouraging collaboration in algorithm design, strategic planning, and resource management. Participants must combine their analytical abilities and technical skills to develop competitive rover controllers and devise effective strategies.

details_text: Event Description Abstract Submission Round Participants must submit an aircraft abstract in A4 format, with 1.5 line spacing and a maximum of 15 pages, along with a ZIP file containing 5–10 construction photographs. The abstract should cover the aircraft design, including dimensions, wing area, estimated flight speed, reservoir and mounting, release mechanism, leakage prevention, centre-of-gravity management, and safe operation. The prescribed format must be downloaded from the respective IIT website and submitted by email at least 20 days before the competition. Shortlisted teams will be announced 15 days before the competition. If multiple teams participate from the same institution, their aircraft designs must be distinct, with at least a 2.5% difference in wingspan, chord, and fuselage length; otherwise, the teams will be disqualified. Qualifier Round The Qualifier Round aims to select the top 30 teams with lightweight aircraft capable of safe, controlled flight carrying a 1,000 mL water payload. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds with the full payload, with no water release required. The water must be stored in a sealed, securely mounted, removable reservoir, with the reservoir and release mechanism included in the aircraft’s empty weight. Judges will inspect the system before takeoff, and there must be no visible leakage. Each attempt must be completed within 3 minutes. Failure to maintain 30 seconds of safe flight or any visible leakage before landing results in a zero score. Each team gets two attempts, with the higher score counted, and only teams that safely complete the loaded flight can advance. The top 30 teams qualify for the Main Round and receive ₹5,000 towards material costs, subject to providing the bank details of one designated team member. Main Round In the Main Round, the aircraft must carry 1,000 mL of water in an inspected, sealed, removable reservoir and release it while flying over the designated simulated fire/release zone. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds before release, which must be manually triggered by the pilot using a single transmitter channel; automatic or programmed release is not allowed. Judges will verify that the release begins within the marked zone, which is approximately 40 m from the take-off/landing area, though its location and dimensions may be adjusted based on venue and wind conditions. The amount of water released will be determined by weighing the reservoir before and after the attempt; if leakage before the commanded release cannot be distinguished from the actual release, the attempt scores zero. Each team gets two attempts, with the better score counted, and each attempt must complete the release and landing within 3 minutes. Rules and Regulations The same aircraft must be used throughout all rounds and must match the submitted design; repairs are allowed, but replacement aircraft are not. Teams should carry spare components and be ready when called, or risk losing their attempt or flight time. A 2.4 GHz radio is required unless another frequency is approved in advance, receivers must remain in receiver mode only, and metal propellers are prohibited. All systems will be inspected before the competition, and non-functional equipment can lead to dismissal. Teams must carry their own equipment and cannot share components with other teams. Aircraft may use powered take-off with landing gear or manual launch. A team member cannot participate in more than one team. Teams must be ready to fly after the 120-second interval following the previous attempt or lose their turn. Reimbursement will only be made to a registered team member whose bank account name matches the registration details. Flying outside the designated zone will result in disqualification, and the aircraft must immediately return and land safely. details_text: Overview Innovate. Build. Break Barriers. About the Hackathon ISTE TCET invites passionate innovators, developers, designers, and problem-solvers to participate in an exciting hackathon that challenges participants to transform ideas into impactful solutions. The hackathon provides a platform for students to collaborate, think creatively, explore emerging technologies, and develop innovative solutions to real-world problems. Whether you are a coder, designer, researcher, or aspiring entrepreneur, this is your opportunity to showcase your skills, experiment with technology, and bring your ideas to life. Work in teams, tackle challenging problem statements, build functional prototypes, and compete with fellow innovators. Push your limits, learn from the experience, and turn your imagination into innovation! Domains Participants can explore innovative solutions across the following domains: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI/ML): Intelligent systems, predictive analytics, automation, generative AI, and AI-powered applications. Web Development: Innovative websites, web applications, SaaS platforms, and digital solutions. Mobile Application Development: Android/iOS applications, cross-platform solutions, and mobile-first innovations. Blockchain & Web3: Decentralized applications, smart contracts, digital identity, and secure transactions. Cybersecurity: Network security, threat detection, data privacy, and secure digital infrastructure. Internet of Things (IoT): Smart devices, automation, connected systems, and sensor-based solutions. Healthcare & MedTech: Healthcare accessibility, patient management, medical innovation, and wellness solutions. FinTech: Digital payments, financial inclusion, banking solutions, and financial automation. Sustainability & Smart Cities: Environmental solutions, waste management, energy efficiency, and smart infrastructure. Open Innovation: Any technology-driven solution addressing a meaningful real-world problem. Participation Guidelines Participation is open to eligible college students. Participants must register within the specified registration deadline. Teams may consist of 2–4 members . Interdisciplinary teams are encouraged. Each team must nominate one team leader as the primary point of contact. All team members must be registered successfully. Hackathon Rules & Regulations All projects must be developed during the designated hackathon period. Pre-existing projects cannot be submitted as original hackathon solutions. However, previously developed libraries, frameworks, and open-source tools may be used. Teams must develop solutions relevant to the selected domain or assigned problem statement. Plagiarism, duplication, and misrepresentation of work will result in disqualification. Teams must submit their source code, project documentation, and working prototype within the stipulated deadline. Participants must ensure that their projects are functional and demonstrable during evaluation. Any use of AI tools, APIs, third-party libraries, and open-source resources must be appropriately acknowledged. Teams must maintain professional conduct throughout the event. details_text: One Who Codes 2026 — Online Portfolio Challenge You already built it. Now show the internet you're one who codes. Participation and claiming a ONEWHO name are free. The challenge is conducted entirely online. Submit a personal portfolio website that represents your own work. How to Participate 1. Deploy Your Portfolio Build your portfolio using your preferred technologies and deploy it on a supported platform: Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Railway, Render, or Fly. 2. Claim Your ONEWHO Name Visit https://isonewho.codes/ , sign in with GitHub, choose your name, and connect your deployed portfolio URL. Your portfolio will be accessible through an address such as: yourname.isonewho.codes 3. Create Your Competition Entry Link Open the Applications section in your ONEWHO dashboard and add an application with the company name “Unstop.” This creates your submission link: https://yourname.isonewho.codes/a/unstop The application link lets you view recorded judging visits and tracked page activity in your ONEWHO dashboard. 4. The public GitHub source repository for your portfolio. Creating a ONEWHO name alone does not complete your competition entry. Your submission must also be completed on Unstop. Content — 20%: How clearly your portfolio communicates who you are, what you build, and the work you have done. Performance and Accessibility — 20%: Loading experience, mobile usability, and accessibility. Rules and Guidelines Each participant may submit only one entry. Templates and AI tools are permitted. Judging rewards your original contribution; changing only the name on a template will not score well on creativity. You must deploy the portfolio yourself on a supported hosting platform. Portfolios automatically generated by ONEWHO from a GitHub profile are not eligible. Submit the required ONEWHO application link and public source repository through Unstop before the deadline. You may improve your portfolio until submissions close. After the deadline, leave the submitted website unchanged until results are announced. Keep your ONEWHO address connected to your portfolio and publicly accessible throughout judging and until results are announced. All entries must comply with ONEWHO’s acceptable use policy: https://isonewho.codes/acceptable-use . Entries that violate the rules or acceptable use policy may be disqualified. details_text: Event Overview WebCloneMania is a web development competition designed to test participants' frontend development, debugging, and problem-solving skills. Beginner Segment – Website Recreation: Participants will recreate a reference website revealed by the organisers at the beginning of the competition, focusing on visual accuracy, responsiveness, and functionality. Advanced Segment – Debug and Deploy: Participants will receive a pre-written codebase containing bugs, incomplete features, and backend issues. Their task is to analyse the code, identify the problems, implement the required fixes, and make the application work correctly. Rules The starter codebase and problem statement will be provided by the organisers at the beginning of the challenge. title: Pixels To Prognosis
description: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different…
details_text: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different radiologists often draw the boundaries differently. Pixels to Prognosis asks you to build an AI system that does this automatically. Using multimodal brain MRI scans, your model has to locate a glioma and separate it into its three subregions: active (enhancing) tumour, necrotic core, and surrounding edema. The event combines neuroscience, MRI physics and computer vision. You’ll need more than a model with a good leaderboard score. You’ll also need to understand what the scans show, why models fail, and how to make one that holds up on real clinical data. Who Can Participate Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any college and any stream Especially suited to students in Biotechnology & Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, and AI & Data Science Teams of 1 to 3 members . Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Quiz (Screening) This is a case-based quiz on: How MRI machines work and the basics of MRI imaging The biology of brain gliomas and how they appear on MRI scans Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Image Processing The questions reward reasoning over memorisation. The quiz is meant to sharpen your problem-solving for the later rounds. Round 2: Model Submission Round Shortlisted teams train a segmentation model on a curated glioma dataset we provide, [derived from the BraTS 2021 challenge]. Each patient has four MRI modalities: T1-weighted, post-contrast T1-weighted (T1ce), T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR. Your model must segment three regions: Whole Tumour, Tumour Core and Enhancing Tumour. Models are ranked on a hidden patient-level test set . Rules: Train only on the dataset provided. No external data. All learnable parameters must start from random initialisation . Pretrained weights are not allowed. You may use published architectures such as U-Net variants. The Colab notebook runtime must be 9 hours or less . Submission requirements: Complete source code (.py / .ipynb) Final trained weights (.pt / .keras) Training logs, including loss and validation curves, config and seed used (.csv) A technical report (.pdf) covering your thought process, pipeline, architecture details and the compute you used Evaluation: Segmentation quality is measured with the Dice score and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance for each tumour region. Scoring also covers anatomical consistency, false-positive control, and the quality of your technical report. Finals: Offline Round at IIT Madras Finalists come to campus and receive a new set of MRI scans with real-world problems. These can include motion artefacts, missing modalities, or pathologies your model has never seen. Each team must: Work out what is wrong with the data and why it happened Adapt the model through preprocessing, retraining or other corrective strategies Present the problems they found, the medical reasoning behind them, and how they handled them Evaluation criteria: Problem identification and medical reasoning Model adaptation strategy and outcome Clarity of presentation and understanding Knowing when your model should not be trusted counts in your favour. Flagging an unreliable case for expert review is part of good clinical AI. Prizes & Recognition Cash prizes for the top 3 teams [prize pool: ₹35000] Special Awards for Best Robust Model and Best Diagnostic Reasoning Certificates of Merit for the winners(Hard Copy) Certificates of Merit for all finalists(Soft Copy) Certificates of Participation for all Round 2 participants Important Dates Registration closes: 28th December, 2026 Round 1 (Online Quiz): 5th December, 2026 Round 2 submission window: 9th - 16th December, 2026 Finals at IIT Madras: 4th January, 2027

title: Agents that act. Systems that answer. | Free Virtual Agentic-AI Hackathon
description: About the Hackathon: Anyone can build an AI demo that works once. Agents that act. Systems that answer. is about what happens when it goes wrong. It's a free, 3-day virtual hackathon for student builders, hosted by…
details_text: About the Hackathon: Anyone can build an AI demo that works once. Agents that act. Systems that answer. is about what happens when it goes wrong. It's a free, 3-day virtual hackathon for student builders, hosted by StudentChakra and co-hosted by Priyanshu Agarwal (founder of NextMove, organiser of Hackorizon). What You'll Build: An agentic AI system for a real person with a real task. Start with a person, not an industry: who are they, what do they hate doing, what does your agent do for them, and where does it break? Solo or in a team of up to 4. No experience required. How Projects Are Judged: We judge how your project behaves when things go wrong: Failure modes: how does it break? Human oversight: who stays in the loop? Intervention: can someone stop it? Reversibility: can a mistake be undone? Plus usefulness to a real person and the quality of your working build. Prizes: $680 in prizes: 1st place about $500 in Apify credits; 2nd and 3rd place Cursor subscriptions. Judges: Experts from AI governance, cybersecurity, venture and OpenAI, including Dr. Esona Fomuso (formerly VP of Technology, JPMorgan Chase), Dr. Aleem Khalid Alvi (Professor of Cybersecurity & Software Engineering, Sheridan College), Kunal Kapoor (Venture Continuity, Katha) and Priyanshu Agarwal (ChatGPT Lab, OpenAI India). Key Dates: Registration closes: Nov 27 Hackathon: Nov 28–30 (virtual) Final results: Dec 8 Who Can Join: Students worldwide, solo or in teams of 1–4. Free.

details_text: About the Event Welcome to Haven Ahmedabad , a beginner-friendly, 24-hour problem-solving game jam tailored specifically for high school students . Scheduled for November 14th to 15th , this event invites programmers, artists, and engineers to spend 24 immersive hours together building fun computer games . Following in the footsteps of major gatherings like Daydream and Campfire Ahmedabad (which was hosted at Ahmedabad University on February 28, 2026, as part of Hack Club's worldwide network of 100 concurrent events and 7,000 attendees) , Haven brings the vibrant energy of global hackathons right to your doorstep. Organized under Hack Club—a 501(c)(3) nonprofit empowering over 50,000 teenagers worldwide to code —this is your space to innovate, create, and collaborate. Our Mission Our mission is to inspire the next generation of makers across Gujarat and beyond by introducing you to game development in a fun, collaborative, and low-stakes environment . Working in teams, you will tackle exciting challenges and build incredible projects that enhance your creativity, collaboration, and innovation skills . For us, hacking is all about problem-solving, making cool projects, and forging lifelong friendships with fellow coders, makers, and artists . Whether you are writing your first line of code or designing your next masterpiece, Haven is designed to help you discover the joy of creating . Why Ahmedabad? Ahmedabad is the ultimate home for Haven . As India's first UNESCO World Heritage City and home to world-class institutions like IIT Gandhinagar, CEPT, and NID, the city has always been a buzzing hub of innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity . Rooted in the local spirit of jugaad (innovative problem-solving) and collaboration—from our historic textile mills to today's thriving startup ecosystem—young makers across neighborhoods from Navrangpura and Satellite to Maninagar and Vastrapur are brimming with potential . Haven Ahmedabad brings together young creators from all over to learn, build, and grow together . What to Expect Beginner-Friendly Atmosphere: No prior game jam experience? No problem! Dive into coding and design in a supportive, low-stakes environment . 24 Hours of Creation: Spend an intense, fun-filled day and night building games, learning from peers, and bringing your ideas to life . Community & Mentorship: Connect with fellow high school coders, artists, and engineers, draw inspiration from your peers, and build lasting friendships . Requirements Demographics: The event is open to high school students (almost all under 18) who are excited to code . title: Drone Soccer | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: A drone soccer competition where teams pilot custom-built, caged drones through an obstacle-filled arena to score points by flying through a circular goal ring. Matches are conducted as timed sprints focusing on agility, defense, and scoring precision.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 5 members; cross-college teams are allowed.
requirements: Custom-built or configured drones with protective cages (no standard RTF models) and the use of only one main drone model.
details_text: Rules & Guidelines: Team Structure: Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 5 members . Cross-college teams are allowed—participants from different institutions can team up. Model Regulations: Each team must use its own custom-built or custom-configured drone wrapped in a protective cage/exoskeleton; exchanging models or components between teams during match rounds is strictly prohibited. Standard RTF (Ready-To-Fly) commercial consumer drones are not allowed, though pre-programmed flight controllers and stabilization boards are permitted. Only one main drone model can be used throughout all competition rounds. Flight and Conduct Rules: No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams will receive a 2-minute warm-up/trial period before Round 2 matches. Lifting or repositioning the drone manually during active gameplay is strictly prohibited. A drone that crashes and is unable to take off within the allotted restart window immediately forfeits that specific attempt or round. The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on all match rules, scoring disputes, and safety calls. Event Structure: Round 1: Drone Soccer Arena Showdown: Obstacle & Defender Navigation: Teams must pilot their caged drones through an active arena featuring physical obstacles and designated opponent defense zones. Goal Scoring Task: Teams must navigate their drone past defensive barricades and maneuver it cleanly through the elevated circular Goal Ring to score points. Each successful goal scored within the match time earns points based on precision and execution. If a goal attempt fails, misses, or bounces off the goal frame, no points are awarded, but no negative penalty is incurred. Teams can immediately reset and attempt another run. Match Execution: Matches are conducted in timed sprints where agility, mid-air defense, collision recovery, and scoring accuracy determine the final winners.

title: Multirotor | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: A two-round drone competition where teams navigate through rings and obstacles to complete a payload delivery task. Participants must fly custom-built drones to score points through precision maneuvering and QR code identification.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 6 members; inter-college teams are permitted.
requirements: A custom-built drone (no RTF models) equipped with an onboard camera for QR scanning.
details_text: Rules: Team Structure: Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 6 members. Participants from different colleges can form a team. Model Regulations: Each team must have its own custom-built drone; exchanging models between teams is strictly prohibited. RTF (Ready-To-Fly) models are not allowed, but pre-programmed boards can be used. Only one model can be used throughout all competition rounds. Flight and Conduct Rules: No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams can have a 2-minute trial before Round 2. Lifting the drone manually to improve position during any round is not allowed. Any failed landing attempt that does not result in a score immediately ends the round. The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on any disputes. Event Structure: Round 1: Teams must fly their drone through 5 circular rings placed at varying heights (between 1 meter to 2.5 meters). Each ring carries different points based on difficulty. Teams must avoid touching the rings to earn points. Skipping a ring results in no points but does not incur a penalty. Maximum time for completion: 8 minutes. Qualification Criteria: Teams with the highest scores will advance to Round 2. Round 2: Obstacle Navigation: Teams must maneuver through multiple obstacles, which will be disclosed on the spot. Payload Task: The onboard camera scans a QR code to identify a specific payload. If scanning fails, teams can receive the QR details manually but will lose detection points. The identified payload must be dropped into a designated area. No penalty for unsuccessful drops, but no points are awarded either.

title: NeuroHack
description: Overview Neurohack is a two-round computational neuroscience hackathon hosted under BIOGEN at SHAASTRA 2027, IIT Madras. Participants will work with real EEG datasets to build pipelines that classify human emotions from…
details_text: Overview Neurohack is a two-round computational neuroscience hackathon hosted under BIOGEN at SHAASTRA 2027, IIT Madras. Participants will work with real EEG datasets to build pipelines that classify human emotions from brainwave signals, combining signal processing, machine learning, and neuroscience in one challenge. Eligibility Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students. Teams of 1–4 members. Participants may be from any discipline and any institute; no prior EEG experience is required, but working knowledge of Python is expected. Target Audience Students interested in: Biotechnology & biomedical engineering Neuroscience and cognitive science Computer science, data science and machine learning Signal processing and electronics Competition Rounds Round 1: Online Quiz An online quiz covering basic neuroscience, EEG principles, brain-wave patterns, and Python for data analysis. Top-scoring teams advance to Round 2. Round 2: 24-Hour Offline Hackathon Selected teams are invited to IIT Madras during SHAASTRA 2027 for a 24-hour hackathon . Participants receive a preprocessed subset of a public EEG emotion dataset and build a complete pipeline to classify human emotions using signal processing and machine learning. Finals at IIT Madras: PPT Presentation Each team presents its problem approach, features, model, results, and insights from the brain signals to a panel of judges, followed by a Q&A session.

title: Shaastra Aerial Robotics Challenge
description: Competition Overview : The Shaastra Aerial Robotics Challenge (SARC) is an exciting drone competition that brings together aspiring engineers, robotics enthusiasts, and innovators to test their drone-building skills,…
details_text: Competition Overview : The Shaastra Aerial Robotics Challenge (SARC) is an exciting drone competition that brings together aspiring engineers, robotics enthusiasts, and innovators to test their drone-building skills, flying precision, and technical knowledge. Participants will navigate challenging obstacle courses, perform precise aerial manoeuvres, and compete in time-based challenges that test their control, stability, accuracy, and problem-solving abilities Competition Rounds: Round 0: Preliminary Submission: Teams must submit a flight demonstration video and a technical PDF for initial evaluation. The video must demonstrate: Smooth take-off and stable hovering. Stable flight while carrying a 50 g payload. Navigation through at least one hoop-shaped obstacle without contact. A precise 90° turn. Safe landing at the designated point. The technical PDF must include drone dimensions, total weight, power source specifications, manual control system details, safety mechanisms, and other relevant technical information. Selected teams will advance to Round 1. Round 1: Obstacle Course Challenge Qualified teams must navigate a specially designed obstacle course while maintaining stable, low-altitude flight. The course includes: Semicircular and quarter hoops. Diagonal split rectangular hoops. Sharp 90° turns. Double quarter hoops. Crossover and split semicircular hoops. Triangular and freely hanging circular hoops. T-rod obstacles. Teams must complete the obstacle sequence, cross the finish line, and land at the designated point. Scoring is based on course completion, time bonuses, and penalties for rule violations. Round 2: Checkpoints Challenge The top-performing teams from Round 1 will qualify for this timed challenge. Reach as many checkpoints as possible within the allotted time. Follow the obstacle-course rules applicable to Round 1. Earn 10 points for each successful checkpoint. Avoid unnecessary contacts and unsafe manoeuvres. The number of qualifying teams will be determined by the organisers based on participation. Round 3: Payload Delivery Challenge Teams will carry an organiser-provided payload through the obstacle course and release it onto a marked target area. Scoring would consider course completion, delivery accuracy, time bonuses, and penalties. Rules and Regulations: Drone type: Only multirotor drones, such as quadcopters and hexacopters, are permitted. Control system: Drones must be operated manually using a remote controller. Autonomous flight is not permitted.3. Dimensions: The drone must not exceed 1 metre and must not be smaller than 0.3 metre in any direction. Flight altitude: Drones must not exceed a height of 1.5 metres and must follow the prescribed arena boundaries and safety-net restrictions. Flight performance: Drones must demonstrate stable hovering, precise low-altitude flight, and controlled manoeuvrability. Obstacle contact: Contact with hoops, rods, will attract penalties. Ground contact: Touching the ground during the course will attract penalties. Arena boundaries: Exiting the arena boundaries may result in disqualification. Unsafe contacts: Exceeding the permitted number of unsafe contacts may result in disqualification. Drone crashes: A crash that prevents continuation may result in disqualification. FPV camera: An FPV camera is optional and is not mandatory. Arena Specifications: Arena dimensions: 8 m × 11 m × 1.25 m. Clearly marked start and finish points will be provided. Obstacle dimensions and placements will have a tolerance of ±5%. Eligibility: Students, robotics enthusiasts, and teams interested in drone technology, aerial robotics, and engineering innovation are encouraged to participate, subject to the final eligibility criteria announced by the organisers. Participants must ensure that their drones comply with the technical specifications and safety requirements. details_text: Overview Krixov presents: AI for Operational Intelligence Case Challenge Build Real. Showcase Skills. Unlock Opportunities. It invites college and university students to analyze real-world operational challenges and propose innovative, practical, data-informed, and responsible AI-enabled solutions. Participants will select one problem statement, analyze its root causes, define the intended users, design a feasible solution, and present their idea through a structured presentation. The challenge focuses on problem-solving, analytical thinking, product innovation, data-driven decision-making, and responsible use of AI. Whether your strengths are technology, business, analytics, design, operations, research, or communication, this is an opportunity to showcase your thinking and present an idea with real-world potential. Event Overview: Event name: BUILD2RISE 2026 Theme: AI for Operational Intelligence Format: Online Competition type: Idea / Case-study presentation Duration: 72 hours (3 days) Problem statements: 6 Participation: Individual or team Team size: 1–4 members Eligibility: Currently enrolled college/university students from any discipline and academic year Submission format: PDF or PowerPoint presentation Rounds: One submission and evaluation round Registration deadline: 15-11-2026 (11:59 PM) Challenge start: 16-11-2026 (12:01 AM) Submission deadline: 18-11-2026 (11:59 PM) Organizer contact: campus@krixov.com Rewards and Recognition: BUILD2RISE 2026 is designed to help students showcase their ideas, strengthen their portfolios, and explore potential career opportunities. 1st and 2nd Place — Top 2 Teams: Internship opportunities Consideration for professional recommendations Winner recognition Opportunity to showcase projects and solutions 3rd, 4th, and 5th Place — Next 3 Teams: Consideration for professional recommendations Recognition among the top-performing teams Opportunity to showcase projects and solutions Other Eligible Participating Teams: - Digital Certificate of Participation for eligible teams that complete the required participation and submission process. Important Reward Terms: Internship opportunities and professional recommendations are subject to eligibility, evaluation, availability, and the organizer’s applicable selection process. They are opportunities for consideration, not a guarantee of an internship, employment, or recommendation. No cash prize is being advertised in this listing. Problem Statements: Participants must select exactly one of the following six problem statements. Problem Statement 1: The Broken Handoff Problem Problem: Work is often delayed when tasks move between departments or team members without complete information, clear ownership, or a defined next action. Challenge: Design a solution that identifies incomplete handoffs, detects missing information, prioritizes tasks at risk of delay, and recommends actions to improve coordination. Expected solution: A workflow-management concept, intelligent checklist, handoff-risk dashboard, or another practical solution. Success measures: Reduced incomplete handoffs, less rework, clearer ownership, and shorter resolution time. Problem Statement 2: The Invisible Cost Detector Problem: Businesses may overlook avoidable operational costs caused by repeated work, unused software licenses, duplicate purchases, and recurring delays. Challenge: Propose a transparent system that identifies potential waste, ranks opportunities for investigation, and estimates possible savings using clear calculations. Expected solution: A cost-intelligence dashboard, expense-analysis system, duplicate-purchase alert, or related concept. Success measures: Better visibility into cost drivers, more reliable identification of potential waste, and transparent savings estimates. Important requirement: Participants must distinguish confirmed waste from uncertain opportunities

Operation Ward Zero is an online healthcare technology hackathon inviting innovators, developers, and problem-solvers to design intelligent home healthcare solutions. Participants will develop a working prototype demonstrating how IoT simulation, full-stack applications, and AI/ML can work together to monitor patient conditions, identify potential risks, and support timely caregiver responses. The central mission is: Sense → Understand → Predict → Alert → Respond Participants are encouraged to develop practical, affordable, scalable, and user-friendly solutions that address real-world home healthcare challenges. No physical hardware is required. Participants may use simulated sensors, synthetic patient data, mock devices, and software-based environments. title: Bazaar: Beat the Markets
description: All that you need to know about EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market Everyone has an opinion on the market. Very few can act on it when prices move every second and the news is half-true. EIC Bazaar…
details_text: All that you need to know about EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market Everyone has an opinion on the market. Very few can act on it when prices move every second and the news is half-true. EIC Bazaar is where you find out which one you are. Organized by the Entrepreneurship & Incubation Cell (EIC) as part of E-Summit, Bazaar is a live stock market trading competition for students. Fictional companies, simulated markets, virtual capital. The pressure is real. What Makes Bazaar Different? Forget static prediction games and paper quizzes. Bazaar runs on a trading platform built specifically for this event, with live prices, breaking news and timed sessions where every decision counts. You don't just trade one market, you trade two. First you play as a retail investor, reading charts and reacting to news. Then you step up to the institutional level, where your own orders move prices, bots trade alongside you, and the market pushes back. News reaches you from many sources: newspapers, analysts, insiders and finfluencers. Not all of them deserve your trust, and knowing which to believe is half the game. The Grand Finale is held at E-Summit, so you compete in the same venue as founders, investors and innovators. Who Should Apply? Bazaar is for anyone who follows the markets, enjoys fast decisions, data or strategy, and wants to experience trading without risking real money. You don't need prior trading experience. Beginners can learn from the rulebook and strategy hints shared before the Finale, and experienced traders will find plenty to exploit. Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students across India. Cross-college teams are welcome. Competition Structure Bazaar runs across two rounds. Round 1 is an Online Quiz on Unstop, covering stock market basics, financial instruments, chart and news reading, and risk-based reasoning. Round 2 is the Grand Finale, held in person at PEC, Chandigarh on 14-15 November as part of E-Summit. Finalists trade on Bazaar's live platform across two stages: Stage 1: Retail. Start with virtual capital. Trade across a range of instruments using technical tools. Trading happens in timed sessions that get tougher as new instruments and news unlock. Stage 2: Institutional. Start fresh with new virtual capital. Now your trades move prices, and bots compete with you for liquidity. Every trade carries a transaction fee, so overtrading will cost you. Teams are ranked on trading performance. General scoring guidelines and a rulebook will be shared with registered teams before the Finale. Team Details Team Size: 2 to 4 members Cross-college and cross-city teams: Fully allowed and encouraged Solo registrations: Not accepted One person registers as Team Leader and adds the remaining members on Unstop Join the WhatsApp Group here.

details_text: Overview Ready to drive the strategic roadmap of an industry giant? Strategy Sprint is the ultimate business case challenge where you step into the role of a C-suite corporate strategist to solve real-world industry transformation puzzles ! Guidelines: Solve High-Stakes Business Case Studies: Analyze major industry shifts, market entry opportunities, and strategic inflection points facing market leaders . Evaluate Strategic Expansion: Weigh key corporate growth decisions like Build, Buy, or Partner —analyzing potential mergers, acquisitions, strategic alliances, or supply chain backward integration . Conduct Deep Financial & Synergies Analysis: Perform cost-benefit evaluations, model expected ROI, assess margin improvements, and justify capital allocations with data-driven financial rigor . Assess Risks & Regulatory Landscape: Map out market risks, technological obsolescence, supply chain vulnerabilities, and policy incentives (like government PLI schemes) . Integrate ESG & Sustainability: Align growth strategies with Net Zero commitments, environmental impact reduction, and long-term ESG performance . Deliver an Actionable Executive Plan: Package your strategic recommendations, 3–5 year implementation roadmap, and quantitative backing into an executive pitch deck ! Platform will be unstop and offline event at IIT Kanpur.

title: Beat The Market | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: This two-round competition challenges participants to build a stock portfolio based on financial analysis and subsequently develop a machine learning model to predict the future prices of those selected stocks.
eligibility: UG and PG college students; teams of up to 5 members.
requirements: Team formation, portfolio construction with financial justification, and machine learning model development.
details_text: Event Structure: Online Round: Portfolio Building & Analysis: All registered teams will receive details of 20 virtual stocks, including their technical and fundamental analysis. Participants must study the stocks and create a portfolio of 8 stocks using a virtual fund of ₹20 lakh. Teams must present a rationale for their selection, supported by financial statements, news articles, or relevant market data. Bonus Challenge: Justify why the remaining 12 stocks were excluded from your portfolio. ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) factors may be incorporated into the portfolio for additional evaluation. Portfolios will be assessed based on stock performance two years into the future, assuming the investments were made in the current year. Offline Round: Machine Learning-Based Stock Price Prediction: Teams will create a Machine Learning model to predict stock prices for each of the 8 selected stocks in their portfolio. A time series model can be used to forecast future price movements. Historical stock data (till Dec 2024) will be provided for training the model. The model will be evaluated on stock prices from 2025-2026. The team with the best-performing model will win the competition. A bonus round will be held, with further details provided on campus. Guidelines: Team Composition & Registration: Each team can have up to 5 members (both UG and PG students are eligible). A participant cannot be part of multiple teams in the same event. Multiple teams from the same college are allowed to participate. Competition & Evaluation: Only college students will be considered when deciding the winners. Teams must justify their portfolio selections with supporting financial data. Machine Learning models will be tested on real stock data from 2025-2026. Rules & Fair Play: The decision of the judges is final and incontestable. The organizers reserve the right to modify the timeline if necessary.

title: Manoeuvre | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: Design and build a manually controlled robot capable of precisely gripping various shapes and inserting them into corresponding grooves on a cubic block.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 6 students, including inter-college teams.
requirements: A custom-built robot with a precise gripping mechanism and a stable wired or wireless control system.
details_text: Task: Bot Design: The bot must be manually controlled and capable of gripping various blocks or shapes. It should be able to insert them into corresponding grooves carved into a cubic block. The gripping mechanism should be precise and able to handle various shapes securely. Control Mechanism: The bot can be either wired or wireless. If wired, the cable should be long enough to ensure it remains slack and does not interfere with the bot’s movement. Wireless control options include a dual-frequency remote, Bluetooth, or Wi-Fi. Task Precision: The bot should be able to precisely align and place the blocks into their respective grooves, requiring accurate control of its movements and gripping mechanism. Flexibility and Range: For wireless bots, ensure the control mechanism provides a stable connection and sufficient range to operate effectively within the task area without any interference or lag. Rules and Regulations: Each team can have a maximum of 6 participants and a minimum of 2 A team may consist of students from different colleges. Teams have to make their robot. They can't use the other team's robot. Certificates of Excellence will be awarded to the top three teams. Judges/organizers' decision will be final.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) How many rounds are in the competition? There are two rounds: an online round followed by a final round where teams/participants compete onsite at Techkriti, IIT Kanpur . How will the winner be decided? Combined scores of Round 1 and Round 2 will be used to determine the winner of the competition . Who will be declared winner in case of a tie? If two or more participants have the same score, the participant who took less time for submission will be given preference .

title: CTF Arena
organiser: International Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Bhubaneswar
description: About Capture The Flag (CTF): A Capture The Flag (CTF) competition is a cybersecurity-based contest where participants solve a variety of real-world hacking challenges to ﬁnd hidden clues called ﬂags. These ﬂags act as…
details_text: About Capture The Flag (CTF): A Capture The Flag (CTF) competition is a cybersecurity-based contest where participants solve a variety of real-world hacking challenges to ﬁnd hidden clues called ﬂags. These ﬂags act as proof of solving a challenge and are submitted on a CTF platform to earn points. Each challenge represents a practical security scenario, encouraging participants to think like ethical hackers while maintaining legal and responsible boundaries. The aim is not just to break systems but to understand, analyze, and defend them that promote both offensive and defensive cybersecurity skills. About the Event: The Capture the Flag (CTF) competition hosted by Tech Society IIIT Bhubaneswar is a cybersecurity challenge designed to test your hacking, analytical, and problem-solving skills in a real-world simulation environment. In this event, participants will face a series of challenges related to ethical hacking domains that include web exploitation, cryptography, forensics, reverse engineering, OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence), steganography, and privilege escalation. Each challenge will test different aspects of cybersecurity knowledge and technical expertise. The event is meant to promote cybersecurity awareness, encourage ethical hacking practices, and create a platform for collaboration among students passionate about security. This event will be conducted offline at IIIT Bhubaneswar, giving participants a chance to interact with cybersecurity enthusiasts, mentors, and experts from different colleges.

details_text: Craft N Code – West Bengal State Qualifier This State Round is exclusively for students studying in colleges across West Bengal. details_text: Overview: Techkriti’27, IIT Kanpur, presents Capture the Flag (CTF) — a cybersecurity competition where participants solve practical security challenges in a simulated real-world environment. Identify vulnerabilities, apply technical problem-solving skills, and capture hidden flags to score points. The competition will challenge participants across areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and vulnerability exploitation , requiring them to choose the right tools and techniques to solve increasingly challenging problems. Guidelines: Team Composition: Participants can compete individually or in teams of up to 2 members. The contest is team-rated, and participants forming a team must register accordingly. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate students, postgraduate students, and professionals worldwide. Only participants who are currently enrolled as university students will be eligible for prizes. Registration & Prize Eligibility: To claim prize money, participants must register on both the competition platform and the Techkriti website. Fair Play & Disqualification: Any form of malpractice or plagiarism will result in immediate disqualification. Participants must follow all competition guidelines. In case of any dispute, the decision of the Techkriti Team, IIT Kanpur, will be final. Rules & Event Structure: Competition Format: The competition will consist of a single round featuring numerous cybersecurity and cryptographic challenges, approximately 8–10. Each challenge will contain a hidden flag, represented as a string of characters, which participants must discover to earn points. The contest will be conducted online and will have a duration of 6 hours. Each problem will be accompanied by a problem statement and relevant code for participants to analyze and work with. Winners will be determined based on their total score. In case of a tie, the participant/team with the faster submission time will be given preference. Difficulty Progression: The challenges will increase in difficulty as the competition progresses, testing participants' ability to identify vulnerabilities, analyze systems, and apply appropriate cybersecurity techniques. Participants may need to demonstrate skills in penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and related areas of cybersecurity. FAQs: Winner in case of a tie: In case two or more participants/teams have the same score, the one with the faster submission time will be given preference. Negative marking: The marking scheme will be announced before the test. Individual participation: Yes. Participants can compete individually or in a team of a maximum 2 members.

description: About the Event: Test your algorithmic trading and game theory skills in Pokerbots, a high-stakes algorithmic bot competition! Teams must code an autonomous Python bot to compete in a custom poker variant designed with…
details_text: About the Event: Test your algorithmic trading and game theory skills in Pokerbots, a high-stakes algorithmic bot competition! Teams must code an autonomous Python bot to compete in a custom poker variant designed with modified Texas Hold’em mechanics to prevent the use of public repositories. Technical & Runtime Constraints: Environment: Python 3.11. Allowed Libraries: Standard Python libraries, NumPy , and SciPy only (no pip installations allowed at runtime) . Compute Limits: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, read-only filesystem, and zero network access . Time Bank: Cumulative time bank per match (~60 seconds for 400 hands) with a hard wall-clock kill. Crashes or exhausted time banks result in match forfeiture. Communication Protocol: Bots operate automatically via a predefined stdin/stdout protocol. Tournament Structure & Progression: All matches utilize duplicate deals (playing every deal twice with swapped seats) to mitigate luck and seat advantage. Stage 1 (Swiss Qualifier): Valid bots play 6 rounds of ~200 duplicate deals (400 hands). Match points: 1 for Win, 0.5 for Draw, 0 for Loss . Stage 2 (Top 32 Finals): The top 32 qualifying teams advance to a full round-robin stage (~500 duplicate deals each). Scores reset prior to this stage. Tie-Breakers: Calculated using a capped chips per hand formula. Rules & Regulations: Team Size: Teams must consist of exactly 2 members . An individual can only be on one team. Submissions: Teams can re-upload/overwrite submissions until November 15th at 23:59 IST . Only the last valid upload counts. Fair Play & Code Review: Code copying, collusion, and network calls are strictly prohibited. Winners' source code will undergo a thorough manual review prior to prize payouts. Evaluation Criteria: Duplicate Deal Performance: Match points accrued during the Swiss Qualifier and final standings in the round-robin stage.

Each conversation features four characters ( A, B, C, and D ), with exactly one character making a statement that contradicts the facts. Using a custom synthetic dataset, your mission is to train a model that spots contradictions with high accuracy. ️ Event Format & Dataset Dataset: Participants receive a custom synthetic dataset containing labeled training data and unlabeled test data. ️ Approach: You may use any Machine Learning or NLP approach—including custom architectures, pretrained models, LLMs, fine-tuning, or rule-based heuristics. Platform: Hosted externally on Kaggle . Rules & Regulations Team Size: Compete individually or in teams of up to 4 members . Submission Limit: Maximum of 5 submissions per team per day on Kaggle. Submission Format: Predictions must be uploaded in the prescribed CSV format before the deadline. Fair Play: Manual labeling of the test dataset and sharing predictions/code between competing teams are strictly prohibited . details_text: About the Event: Slay CTF is a thrilling, jeopardy-style Capture The Flag competition designed to test your offensive security skills, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Whether you are a beginner looking to break into the world of cybersecurity or a seasoned hacker hunting for complex challenges, Slay CTF offers a dynamic environment to exploit vulnerabilities, crack ciphers, and trace digital footprints. Put your skills to the test, climb the global leaderboard, and prove your mettle in the ultimate battle of bits and bytes! Eligibility & Registration Guidelines: Target Audience: Open to all students (UG/PG/Diploma), early-career professionals, and self-taught security enthusiasts. Inter-College Teams: Allowed and highly encouraged. Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed (Open to all branches and backgrounds). Team Size: Participate individually or in teams of [1 - 3 members] . Prerequisites: Eagerness to learn. Challenge Categories (Topics) The CTF will feature a diverse set of challenges scaled from beginner to advanced difficulties across the following domains: Web Exploitation: Uncover vulnerabilities in web applications (e.g., SQLi, XSS, IDOR, SSRF). OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence): Track down hidden information and piece together digital trails across the public internet. Cryptography: Break encryption schemes, decode ciphers, and analyze cryptographic protocols. Digital Forensics: Analyze memory dumps, network packet captures (PCAPs), and hidden file metadata. Reverse Engineering: Deconstruct compiled binaries and understand their underlying logic. Miscellaneous / Sanity: Brain-teasers, scripting challenges, and out-of-the-box puzzles. Event Format & Process Format: Hybrid (Online + JGEC Campus), Jeopardy-Style CTF. Platform: Challenges will be hosted on our dedicated infrastructure ( CTFd). Duration: The competition will run continuously for 3 hours . Scoring System: Dynamic scoring will be implemented (the point value of a challenge decreases as more teams solve it). Process: Once registered on Unstop, team leaders will receive the platform link and credentials via email 24 hours prior to the event kickoff. Rules & Code of Conduct No Flag Sharing: Sharing flags or solutions with other teams is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification of all involved parties. No Brute-Forcing: Automated brute-forcing of the flag submission platform or challenge infrastructure is forbidden unless explicitly mentioned in the challenge description. No Attacking the Infrastructure: Do not launch Denial of Service (DoS/DDoS) attacks or attempt to compromise the hosting servers. Collaboration: You are free to use Google, AI tools, and public documentation, but collaboration is strictly limited to your own team members. Final Decisions: The organizing team's decisions regarding scoring, disputes, and disqualifications are final and binding. Prizes & Perks Cash Prize, Certification Vouchers and goodies. [NOTE: Cash Prizes and Goodies exclusively for offline participation] Official Certificate of Participation for those who solve at least one challenge.
