title: AETHOS - Day Zero
description: If civilization had to begin again tomorrow, what would humanity build first? Unlike conventional hackathons that ask participants to build products around a technology, DAY ZERO challenges teams to engineer the…
details_text: If civilization had to begin again tomorrow, what would humanity build first? Unlike conventional hackathons that ask participants to build products around a technology, DAY ZERO challenges teams to engineer the foundations of an entirely new civilization. Participants are encouraged to think beyond applications and incremental improvements. Every project should solve a meaningful challenge that contributes to rebuilding society—whether through communication, energy, healthcare, infrastructure, education, resilience, exploration, or entirely new approaches that redefine the future. This is not about recreating yesterday. It is about engineering tomorrow. The Mission: Design and develop an innovative solution that would help humanity rebuild after the collapse of modern civilization. Your project may be software, hardware, embedded systems, IoT, AI, robotics, communication systems, cybersecurity, biotechnology, space technology, sustainable engineering, or any interdisciplinary solution aligned with the mission. Projects should focus on solving real-world problems with practical engineering, long-term scalability, and meaningful societal impact. Civilization Pillars: Every project belongs to one of the official Civilization Pillars that represent the essential functions required to rebuild society. The detailed descriptions of all pillars are provided separately. Choose the pillar that best represents the purpose of your solution, not simply the technologies you use. Who Can Participate? Students from any recognized institution are welcome. Participants from all engineering, science, technology, design, management, and interdisciplinary backgrounds are encouraged. Teams must follow the team size specified on the registration page. Innovation thrives when diverse disciplines work together. What Can You Build? We welcome projects across a wide range of domains, including but not limited to: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Embedded Systems & Electronics Internet of Things (IoT) Robotics & Automation Wireless Communication Systems Healthcare & Medical Technologies Renewable Energy Smart Infrastructure Disaster Management Cybersecurity Space & Aerospace Technologies Sustainability Human-Centered Design Frontier & Moonshot Innovations If your solution contributes meaningfully to rebuilding civilization, it belongs here. Submission Requirements: Teams should be prepared to submit: Project presentation Technical documentation Source code repository Prototype or proof of concept Demonstration video (if applicable) Additional submission guidelines and templates will be shared with registered participants. Evaluation: Projects will be assessed on their overall contribution toward rebuilding civilization, including: Innovation Engineering excellence Technical feasibility Scalability Societal impact Resilience Quality of presentation The complete judging rubric is available in the attached documentation. General Rules: All submitted work must be original. Open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools may be used with proper attribution. AI-assisted development is permitted unless otherwise specified. Plagiarism or intellectual property violations will result in immediate disqualification. Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and uphold the event's code of conduct. Decisions made by the organizing committee and judging panel will be final. A comprehensive rulebook is available in the attached resources. Why Participate? DAY ZERO is more than a competition. It is an opportunity to think like the engineers who would shape the first generation of a new civilization. Challenge assumptions. Collaborate across disciplines. Build technologies that matter. Engineer systems that could redefine humanity's future. Tomorrow Begins Here. History remembers the civilizations that were built. The next one starts with your idea.

details_text: Short Description: Escape the corporate hustle and step into the vibrant, green ecosystem of IIM Bangalore! Join us for a guided bird-watching walk and workshop designed to explore urban biodiversity, avian life, and the symbiotic relationship between nature and sustainable practices. Detailed Event Overview & About the Workshop: Drishti 2026 presents Birding Buddies — an immersive nature walk and interactive workshop hosted amidst the sprawling, biodiverse campus of the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB). Whether you are a seasoned birding enthusiast or a curious beginner, this session offers a unique blend of outdoor exploration, biodiversity awareness, and environmental reflection. Key Highlights: Guided Campus Trail: Explore IIM Bangalore’s famous flora and fauna, home to over 80+ recorded species of birds, insects, and native trees. Hands-on Bird Identification: Learn how to use field guides, binoculars, and bird-call detection apps like eBird and Merlin. Interactive Classroom Discussion: Reflect on avian behaviour, urban sustainability, and why preserving green corridors matters in modern city planning. Networking & Rejuvenation: Connect with fellow nature lovers, students, and working professionals over a light networking breakfast. Schedule: Stage 1: Registration & Campus Access Eligibility: Open to all students, corporate professionals, and nature enthusiasts. Mode: Offline (IIM Bangalore Campus) Stage 2: Event Day Schedule on 14 November 2026 Time Slot Activity Details 06:30 AM – 08:00 AM IIM-B Campus Bird Walk Guided nature trail across key campus biodiversity spots led by expert naturalists. 08:00 AM – 08:30 AM Breakfast & Rejuvenation Networking break over healthy breakfast (included in registration fee). 08:30 AM – 10:00 AM Interactive Workshop & Reflection Classroom session mapping species spotted, discussion on urban bird conservation, and Q&A. Eligibility & Rules: Participation Type: Individual Who Can Register: Open to undergraduate/postgraduate students, school students, working professionals, and nature enthusiasts. What to Bring: Comfortable walking shoes & muted-colored clothing. Binoculars (optional, but recommended). A refillable water bottle. Code of Conduct: Maintain quietness on the trails so as not to disturb wildlife. Do not litter or disrupt the natural habitat during the walk. Registration Fee & Deliverables Registration Fee: ₹299 per participant Inclusions: Guided walk with naturalists. Entry to classroom workshop session. Complimentary breakfast & refreshments. Certificate of Participation from Drishti 2026, IIM Bangalore.

description: Overview Take a Seat at IIMB: Marketing in a World of Clones: Creating Differentiation and Competitive Advantage to Stand Out from the Crowd Step into a live IIM Bangalore classroom and learn alongside India’s top…
details_text: Overview Take a Seat at IIMB: Marketing in a World of Clones: Creating Differentiation and Competitive Advantage to Stand Out from the Crowd Step into a live IIM Bangalore classroom and learn alongside India’s top executive MBA cohort We live in a world of intense competition, where product quality is often taken for granted and standing out is harder than ever. What are customers really buying? Why do some companies struggle to differentiate themselves, while others consistently capture attention and build a lasting competitive advantage? In this session, Prof. Ramesh Venkateswaran explores the principles of marketing differentiation, examining how successful companies distinguish themselves, create meaningful value for customers, and rise above the competition. Join this live IIM Bangalore class at Drishti 2026 on Saturday, 14 November, from 11:45 AM to 1:15 PM, and discover what it takes to stand out in a world of clones. About the opportunity Ever wondered what it is like to study at IIM Bangalore? “Take a Seat at IIMB” gives you the chance to sit in on a live class with the Post Graduate Programme in Enterprise Management (PGPEM) cohort — IIMB’s executive MBA, ranked No. 1 in India by the Financial Times and QS. This session is using IIMB’s case-based, discussion-driven teaching. You will learn alongside working professionals averaging around 13 years of experience, and see first-hand how real business problems are debated and decided in an IIM classroom. What you will experience A live Leadership class with an IIM Bangalore faculty member The case method in action: preparation, debate and decision-making Perspectives from experienced professionals across 15+ industries in the PGPEM cohort A short interaction with PGPEM participants about life and learning at IIMB Who should participate Working professionals considering an executive MBA Students and aspiring MBA applicants who want to experience an IIM classroom Lifelong learners curious about IIMB’s teaching style Format & schedule Pre-reading (case or note) shared by email before the session Saturday, 14 November, from 11:45 AM to 1:15 PM Arrive 30 minutes early for check-in and seating Participate as an observer, with the option to contribute where invited by the faculty Post-class interaction with PGPEM participants What you get A seat in a live IIM Bangalore class Certificate of participation from Drishti 2026, IIM Bangalore Interaction with the PGPEM cohort Access to Drishti 2026 sessions at IIMB Auditorium Eligibility & rules Open to working professionals and students (UG/PG) aged 18 and above. Participants must follow classroom etiquette: punctuality, phones on silent, no recording. The case and class materials are for personal use only and may not be shared. Carry a valid photo ID for campus entry. Registration is confirmed only on successful payment on Unstop; seats are first-come, first-served. Fees are non-refundable; the organisers’ decision on all matters is final. About Drishti 2026 Drishti is the annual business-cum-cultural summit of IIM Bangalore, organised by the students of the Post Graduate Programme in Enterprise Management (PGPEM), IIMB’s executive MBA ranked No. 1 in India by the Financial Times and QS. The 2026 edition, themed “India 2047: Decisive Moves for the Next Decades”, takes place on 13–14 November 2026 at the IIM Bangalore campus and brings together senior executives, domain experts and future leaders across public policy, AI, manufacturing, international trade, R&D and sustainability.

Stand out from the crowd in job applications by flaunting your certificate from Shaastra, IIT Madras! Gear up to be a champion in competitions by building strong fundamentals! Learn from the masters of the trade who have proved their mettle This workshop explores how natural architectures—like bird nests and coral reefs—inspire advanced additive manufacturing for construction and automotive applications . Participants will examine fundamental layer-by-layer principles, CAD modeling, slicing, and key AM hardware components . Major processes covered include SLA, FDM, SLS, and Directed Energy Deposition, alongside Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) using polymers, metals, and ceramics . Attendees will explore real-world applications, process limitations, emerging research like digital twins, and characterization techniques . The curriculum culminates in practical insights into post-processing and print defect diagnosis. details_text: Overview Stronger Collaboration Between Technical Institutions and Industry There is an urgent need for stronger collaboration between technical institutions and industry. All that you need to know about Techfest Prompt Engineering Workshop Prompt Engineering Workshop: Prompt Engineering is the practice of turning a raw AI model into a precise, reliable tool  structuring instructions well enough to get accurate, consistent, and usable output every single time. It sits at the intersection of human intent and AI systems, going far beyond "how to talk to ChatGPT" to cover grounding prompts in real data, multimodal inputs, and prompt security  the exact standards enterprise AI teams work with in 2026. Today, this skill is being demanded across every function, not just tech roles: software, finance, healthcare, marketing, legal, and education are all pairing domain expertise with the ability to drive AI effectively, a combination that pays a premium over either skill alone. From building multi-step reasoning chains to structuring content so AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude actually cite it (Generative Engine Optimization, the AI-era equivalent of SEO), businesses now run on well-engineered prompts, not lucky guesses  and this workshop teaches you to build them. Across two intensive offline days at IIT Bombay, you'll go from foundational prompt structures to a real, evaluated prompt system you'll design, test, and refine yourself  no prior AI or coding background required. Workshop Content Foundations of Prompt Engineering Prompt Structuring & Response Shaping Context, Memory & RAG Domain-Specific & Multimodal Prompting Zero-Shot & Few-Shot Learning Advanced Prompting: Chaining & Reasoning Patterns Adaptive & Self-Optimizing Prompt Systems Prompt Security & Evaluation AI Search & GEO Capstone: Build & Test Systems + Certification

description: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline…
details_text: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline (Concept Sessions, Live Demos & Hands-On Practice) Limited Seat available: About the Workshop Agentic AI represents the biggest paradigm shift in applied artificial intelligence since basic chatbots. Modern enterprise solutions are rapidly evolving from simple single-turn systems to fully autonomous, tool-using agents capable of planning, deciding, and acting. This intensive 2-day hands-on workshop covers the entire agent lifecycle—from core reasoning loops and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to multi-agent orchestration, safety guardrails, and real-world deployment. Participants will build functional agents from scratch using industry-standard frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Why You Should Attend: Master Next-Gen Tech: Deep-dive into the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—the open standard for connecting models directly to enterprise tools and data. Hands-On Experience: Build, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end agents with real-world execution. Framework Mastery: Gain direct technical exposure to LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and vector database integrations. Production-Grade Design: Learn memory management, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) checkpoints, system safety, and token-cost optimization. Workshop Syllabus & Core Topics: Agentic Foundations & Architectures: Transition from chatbots to autonomous agents, master the Sense-Think-Act-Reflect loop, explore operational autonomy levels, and identify failure mitigation strategies. LLM Integration & Prompting: Optimize context windows, implement function calling with JSON schema structured outputs, design production-grade system prompts, and analyze model speed/cost trade-offs. Reasoning & Planning Patterns: Implement multi-step reasoning patterns including ReAct, Reflexion, and Tree-of-Thought alongside automated task decomposition and Orchestrator-Worker routes. Tool Execution & Safety Checkpoints: Design robust tool schemas for deterministic APIs, handle errors with auto-retries, optimize execution (parallel vs. sequential), and integrate Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) safety checks. Model Context Protocol (MCP): Build, connect, and sandbox custom MCP servers using standard Host/Client/Server architecture, primitives, and transport mechanisms (stdio vs. HTTP/SSE). Memory Management & RAG Pipelines: Architect dynamic short-term context and persistent long-term memory using vector databases, context engineering, dynamic session state, and high-retrieval RAG. Multi-Agent Systems & Frameworks: Construct peer-to-peer and hierarchical agent topologies using state handoffs, while comparing leading frameworks: LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Capstone Build & Deployment: Hands-on experience building, debugging, benchmarking, and applying guardrails to deploy a production agent as an API, Web App, or Chat Interface.

title: International Conference on Sustainability Through Digital Transformation
description: The International Conference on "Sustainability through Digital Transformation: Insights from Management, Humanities, Science and Social Science" is organized by Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions (MPGI) with…
details_text: The International Conference on "Sustainability through Digital Transformation: Insights from Management, Humanities, Science and Social Science" is organized by Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions (MPGI) with generous grant support from Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Azad Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow. The twin imperatives of our time — achieving sustainable development and harnessing rapid digital transformation — can no longer be addressed in isolation. Emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain, Internet of Things, and Cloud Computing are reshaping how organizations, governments, and communities pursue economic, social, and environmental goals. At the same time, the pursuit of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) demands insights that cut across disciplinary boundaries — from business strategy and public policy to ethics, culture, scientific innovation, and social behaviour. This conference provides a common platform for academicians, researchers, industry practitioners, policymakers, and research scholars from India and abroad to deliberate on how digital transformation can be leveraged as a catalyst for sustainability. By bringing together perspectives from Management, Humanities, Science, and Social Science, the conference seeks to foster interdisciplinary dialogue, encourage collaborative research, and generate actionable insights for building a resilient, inclusive, and digitally empowered sustainable future. Selected papers will be considered for publication in conference proceedings / reputed journals (details to be announced).

details_text: Masters’ Union Nations ’26 ZERO: THE WORLD RESET Dates: 28–29 November 2026 Venue: CDS Corporate Towers, Gurugram, Haryana Format: Offline | Two-Day Experiential Conference About the Conference Masters’ Union Nations ’26 is a two-day experiential student conference that brings together ambitious young minds from diverse schools and backgrounds to debate ideas, challenge perspectives, and engage with real-world challenges. Built around the theme “ZERO: THE WORLD RESET,” the conference goes beyond the traditional MUN format by combining diplomacy, politics, finance, journalism, corporate strategy, sports management, and entrepreneurship. Participants will have the opportunity to develop leadership, public speaking, critical thinking, negotiation, teamwork, and strategic decision-making skills while collaborating and competing with students from different backgrounds. Committees and Simulations 1. United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) Address critical human rights concerns, including human trafficking, forced labour, and exploitation, with a focus on conflict-affected regions. Delegates will engage in diplomacy, policy discussions, and negotiations to develop solutions. 2. The Eternal Court Enter a fictional world thrown into chaos following the assassination of Death. Participants must navigate a collapsing cosmic order through strategic arguments, alliances, and crisis-driven decision-making. 3. IPL Auction Simulation Build a competitive cricket franchise through a live auction. Participants must manage a fixed purse, evaluate players, plan squad composition, and make strategic bidding decisions. 4. International Press Step into the role of a journalist, photographer, investigator, caricaturist, or newsroom contributor. Cover committee proceedings, investigate developments, and communicate the conference's biggest stories. 5. Dalal Street Simulation Experience a simulated stock market shaped by breaking news and evolving market conditions. Participants must analyse developments, make investment decisions, manage risk, and aim to maximise their portfolio's performance. 6. Committee on Corporate Engagement and Policy Making (CCEP) Work in teams to navigate corporate auctions, funding decisions, crisis management, and strategic discussions involving businesses and policymakers. 7. All India Political Parties Meet (AIPPM) Engage in political debate surrounding the Uniform Civil Code, gender justice, secularism, religious freedom, and constitutional rights. Participants will defend positions, challenge opposing arguments, and explore policy implications. 8. Boardroom Think like an entrepreneur by developing startup concepts, making strategic business decisions, and presenting ideas in an experiential boardroom environment. Eligibility The conference is intended for university and school students interested in diplomacy, politics, business, economics, finance, journalism, entrepreneurship, and related fields. Both experienced MUN delegates and first-time participants are welcome to explore the opportunity. Participants should be prepared to engage respectfully, collaborate with fellow delegates, and contribute actively to their assigned committee or simulation. Conference Format The conference will take place over two days, featuring committee sessions and immersive simulations. Participants will engage in discussions, negotiations, strategic exercises, crisis scenarios, and other activities relevant to their assigned committee. Committee-specific agendas, procedures, allocation details, and schedules will be communicated by the organising team through official conference updates. Participation Guidelines Participants are expected to maintain professional conduct, respect differing viewpoints, follow committee-specific procedures, and comply with instructions issued by the organising team and committee authorities. Plagiarism, disruptive behaviour, harassment, or any conduct that compromises the experience of other participants

About the Faculty of Law: The Faculty of Law at Kalinga University, Naya Raipur, is committed to promoting academic excellence and professional development in legal education. With a team of distinguished scholars and experienced faculty members, it provides students with a balanced blend of theoretical knowledge and practical skills required to succeed in the evolving legal profession. Its curriculum is designed to address contemporary legal challenges, enabling students to develop the knowledge and competencies needed to navigate the complexities of today's legal landscape. About the Two-Day Global Conference: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies, reshaping legal systems across the world. From automated decision-making in commercial transactions and predictive policing to AI-generated intellectual property and algorithmic tools in judicial processes, AI continues to redefine governance and legal frameworks. While these technologies promise greater efficiency, innovation, and improved access to justice, they also raise significant concerns relating to accountability, transparency, bias, privacy, liability, and the protection of fundamental human rights. As AI technologies continue to evolve, legal systems across different jurisdictions are adopting diverse regulatory approaches. Questions surrounding the authorship of AI-generated works, criminal liability for autonomous systems, algorithmic discrimination in courts, data protection in healthcare technologies, cross-border cyber risks, and international norms governing autonomous weapons have intensified the need for comparative legal dialogue. The absence of uniform global standards further complicates enforcement, jurisdictional accountability, and regulatory harmonisation. Understanding these multidimensional challenges is essential for developing coherent and future-ready legal frameworks. Comparative legal analysis enables policymakers, researchers, and legal scholars to identify best practices, bridge regulatory gaps, and formulate adaptive legal responses. Commercial law, criminal justice, intellectual property, judicial institutions, healthcare regulation, cyber law, and international legal mechanisms must evolve in a balanced manner that promotes innovation while safeguarding constitutional values and human dignity. Centred on the theme “India 2047: Decisive Moves for the Next Decades,” Day 1 brings together conversations on the future of AI, human potential, and India's journey towards becoming a global leader. From exploring the human imperative in an AI-driven world to envisioning India's growth towards 2047, the day blends thought-provoking discussions with engaging experiences, learning, and celebration. With workshops, a keynote address, a stand-up comedy act, and an alumni networking dinner, Day 1 offers opportunities to learn, connect, and be inspired. Inauguration Ceremony 2:30 PM – 3:15 PM Drishti 2026 officially opens with an inaugural song and dance performance, followed by the Chairperson’s address. The ceremony sets the stage for two days of ideas, competition, culture, and conversations about India's future. Chief Guest Address 3:15 PM – 4:00 PM Hear from our Chief Guest as they share perspectives on leadership, ambition, and the opportunities that will shape India's journey towards 2047. This session sets the context for the conversations and ideas that define Drishti 2026. Panel Discussion: The Human Imperative — Purpose, Creativity and Agency in the Age of AI 4:20 PM – 5:20 PM As artificial intelligence reshapes industries and the nature of work, what remains uniquely human? This panel explores the evolving relationship between technology and people, examining the role of purpose, creativity, critical thinking, and individual agency in an increasingly AI-driven world. Discover how organisations and individuals can embrace technological progress while keeping human potential at the centre of transformation. Keynote Address: India 2047 5:30 PM – 6:30 PM What will it take for India to realise its aspirations by 2047? This keynote explores the opportunities, challenges, and decisive choices that could shape India's next two decades. From innovation and economic growth to leadership and long-term national priorities, the session invites participants to think beyond the present and imagine the India we can collectively build. Comedy: Stand-Up Comic Act 6:45 PM – 7:45 PM Unwind after an inspiring day of conversations and ideas with a lively stand-up comedy act. Bringing humour, wit, and entertainment to the Drishti stage, this session offers participants a chance to relax, share a laugh, and enjoy the lighter side of the fest. Be part of Drishti 2026! Register now to experience a day of ideas that inspire action. Venue: IIM Bangalore Auditorium, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru Dates: 13–14 November 2026

details_text: Overview Day 2 of Drishti 2026 continues the journey towards imagining and shaping India's future. details_text: Competition Description: Do you have the creativity, precision, and technical skills to transform an engineering idea into a 3D model under time pressure? Welcome to Speed Modelling, an exciting CAD challenge where engineering design meets speed and accuracy! Participants will be given a mechanical component, reference image, or engineering drawing and must recreate its 3D model using CAD software within the allotted time. The challenge is to interpret the given reference, visualize the geometry, and construct an accurate digital model using appropriate modelling tools and techniques. From basic geometric features to intricate mechanical components, every modelling operation counts. Participants will be evaluated on dimensional accuracy, geometric precision, modelling approach, and completion time. Can you turn a design into a precise 3D model before the clock runs out? Visualize. Model. Conquer! Competition Format: Participation: Individual Duration: As specified by the organizers. Software: CAD software specified by the organizers (e.g., CATIA, SolidWorks, or Fusion 360). Challenge: Create a 3D model of the given mechanical component using the provided reference. Evaluation: Dimensional accuracy, geometric precision, completeness, and time management. Winning Criteria: Highest overall score based on modelling accuracy and completion. Rules And Regulations: Each participant must independently create the assigned 3D model using the designated CAD software. A reference image, engineering drawing, or component geometry will be provided at the beginning of the competition. Participants must complete the assigned model within the allotted time. Only the CAD software and tools approved by the organizers may be used. Participants must work independently. Collaboration, communication with other participants, or external assistance is prohibited. Use of pre-existing CAD models, downloaded files, or ready-made templates for the assigned component is strictly prohibited. Participants must save their work in the designated file format and submit it before the deadline. The model must represent the given component accurately, including its major geometric features and dimensions. Participants must not use mobile phones, the internet, or external references unless explicitly permitted. Any technical issues must be immediately reported to the event coordinators. The organizers’ decisions regarding evaluation, rule violations, and final results will be binding. Judging Criteria: Evaluation Parameter Weightage Dimensional Accuracy 30% Geometric Accuracy and Completeness 25% Modelling Approach and Feature Utilization 20% Time Management 15% File Organization and Final Submission 10% Total 100% Winner Selection: Participants will be ranked based on their cumulative scores across all evaluation parameters. The participant achieving the highest score in the final round will be declared the winner. In case of a tie, the participant who completes the model with greater accuracy in lesser time may be given preference. details_text: Pitch Your Idea. Prove Its Worth. Win the Deal! About The Competition: Every successful business begins with an idea. But can you turn yours into a viable venture? SHARK TANK is an entrepreneurial pitching competition that challenges aspiring innovators and future entrepreneurs to present their startup ideas, innovative products or business solutions before a panel of judges – the Sharks. Participants must identify a real-world problem, propose an innovative solution, demonstrate its business potential and convince the Sharks why their idea deserves recognition and investment. Think creatively, pitch confidently and prove that your idea has what it takes to make an impact! Competition Format: Participation: Individual / Team-based Team Size: 2–4 members Pitch Duration: 5–7 minutes Q&A Session: 3–5 minutes Presentation: PPT / Live Demonstration / Prototype Domains: Startups, Engineering Innovations, Technology, Sustainability, Social Entrepreneurship and Business Solutions. Competition Stages: Stage 1: Idea Submission & Screening: Participants submit a brief abstract of their proposed startup idea. Entries are evaluated on originality, problem relevance, innovation and feasibility. Shortlisted participants advance to the final round. Stage 2: The Grand Pitch – 6 November 2026: Shortlisted participants pitch their ideas before the Sharks. Each team gets 5–7 minutes to present, followed by a 3–5-minute Q&A session. Winners are selected based on the final judging scores. Suggested Pitch Structure: Participants should cover: Problem Identification Proposed Solution Innovation & Unique Selling Proposition (USP) Target Market Business Model & Revenue Generation Market Potential Financial Viability Scalability & Impact Investment Ask Rules & Regulations: Ideas must be original and address a clearly identified problem or market need. Participants must explain the solution, its uniqueness and business potential. Market research, financial projections and validation claims must be accurate. PPTs, prototypes and live demonstrations are permitted. Participants must adhere to the allotted presentation time. All team members must contribute and be prepared for the Q&A session. Plagiarism or misrepresentation of ideas will lead to disqualification. External data and references must be appropriately acknowledged. The decisions of the judging panel and organizing committee will be final. Judging Criteria: Evaluation Parameter Weightage Innovation & Originality 20% Problem Identification & Relevance 15% Technical & Business Feasibility 20% Market Potential & Scalability 15% Financial Viability & Business Model 15% Pitching Skills & Q&A 15% Total 100% Winner Selection & Prizes: Winners will be selected based on their cumulative scores across all judging parameters. Exciting prizes and certificates will be awarded to the winning participants/teams. Certificates of participation will be provided to eligible participants. Ready To Face The Sharks?: Bring your boldest idea, back it with a solid strategy and pitch it with confidence. The Sharks are listening. The deal is yours to win!

details_text: AstroPixel: The Night Sky Photography Competition The night sky has fascinated people for as long as we’ve looked up. A single frame can hold the Milky Way arching over a quiet landscape, a trail of stars circling the pole, or the soft glow of a distant nebula. AstroPixel is a competition for people who chase that kind of image. About the Competition AstroPixel invites photographers, students and hobbyists to submit their best astrophotography and compete for recognition. Whether you shoot with a DSLR on a tripod, a mirrorless camera with a fast lens, a tracking mount and telescope, or a smartphone with night mode, you are welcome here. We care about what you capture and how thoughtfully you capture it, not how expensive your gear is. How Entries Are Judged Entries will be judged on creativity (originality, composition and storytelling) and technical skill (focus, exposure, noise control and processing), weighted equally. Rules and Guidelines All work must be your own, captured by you. Each participant may submit up to 1 image. Heavy manipulation, such as adding stars or objects that were not in the original scene, is not allowed. Standard adjustments like stacking, noise reduction, curves and color correction are fine. Include a short caption with each entry: location, date, and camera and lens or telescope used. A brief note on your process is a bonus. Grab your camera, find a dark sky, and show us the universe through your lens.

title: Math Sprint
description: No opponents, no luck: just you and the questions. Math Sprint is a live online Maths challenge on Mind Race (mindrace.in). Everyone starts together and solves questions one by one, on their own. The questions adapt to…
details_text: No opponents, no luck: just you and the questions. Math Sprint is a live online Maths challenge on Mind Race (mindrace.in). Everyone starts together and solves questions one by one, on their own. The questions adapt to you: get them right and they get harder; get stuck and they get easier. Everyone is tested at their own level, and the leaderboard shows who is really the strongest. When: Saturday, 14 November · 8:00–9:00 PM IST Subject: Mathematics Where: Online at mindrace.in, on your phone or laptop Entry: Free, individual How to take part Register here on Unstop. Important: the event is played on Mind Race, so registering on Unstop alone is not enough. Before 14 Nov, create your free Mind Race account, verify your email and join the event here: mindrace.in/e/FXZNEG?ref=unstop (event code FXZNEG ). At 8:00 PM, open the event and press Start . How it works Answer questions one at a time until 9:00 PM. Each question has its own timer, from 30 seconds for easy ones to 90 seconds for the hardest. Attempt at least 75 questions to be ranked. Skips and time-outs count as attempts. That's under 48 seconds per question, so keep moving. You're ranked by your Mind Score : the skill your answers prove. Hard questions solved count for more, and a careless mistake on an easy one costs a lot. Answering more makes your score more certain, not bigger, so accuracy beats rushing. You can skip at most 1 question in 3. A skip counts as half a wrong answer, and the next question won't be easier. The leaderboard freezes for the last 5 minutes. You can't start after 8:50 PM. Prizes ₹200 · ₹150 · ₹100 Amazon vouchers A certificate of participation for everyone who attempts 75 questions Fair play Solve it yourself: no calculator, AI, search engine or help from anyone. One player, one account, one device. We check the timing and accuracy of every answer. Before winners are announced, top players may be asked to solve a few questions live on Google Meet with camera, mic and screen sharing on. Anyone caught cheating loses their result and prize and is banned from Mind Race for 3 days.

details_text: ANAVARAN, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is an immersive sustainability investigation and strategy competition that challenges participants to uncover the gap between corporate sustainability claims and ground realities. Teams of four step into the roles of Sustainability Investigators and Corporate Strategists, investigating Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd., a fictional organisation whose green image may not reflect its actual environmental and social impact. Across three challenging rounds, participants will identify greenwashing, investigate hidden contradictions, assess business risks and develop commercially viable sustainability strategies under real-world-inspired crises. From questioning environmental claims to defending strategic decisions before a jury, ANAVARAN tests critical thinking, ESG awareness, analytical ability and the power to build a genuinely sustainable future. ROUND 1 – GREEN OR GREENWASH? Spot the Illusion Teams will receive a collection of fictional ESG claims, advertisements, sustainability statements, corporate announcements and certification claims made by Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. regarding its proposed Hooghly Data Park in West Bengal. Participants must critically examine each of the 10 claims and classify them into one of three categories: Genuine Sustainability Greenwashing Misleading Communication Each classification must be supported by a short justification explaining what is being promised, whether the claim is verifiable, what important information is missing and whether the communication creates an exaggerated positive impression. Round Details: Mode: Online on Unstop. Format: ESG Claim Classification + Justification Brief. Case: Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. – Hooghly Data Park. Number of Claims: 10. Submission: Each claim must include its classification and a justification of 3–6 lines. Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2. Teams must investigate the contradictions between the company's public sustainability commitments and its internal operational realities. Participants must identify instances of greenwashing, uncover misleading disclosures, assess environmental and social implications, and evaluate the financial, regulatory and reputational risks arising from these gaps. Teams will present their investigation findings and risk assessment before the jury. Round Details: Mode: Offline. Timing: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM (as specified in the event brochure). Format: Case Investigation + Jury Findings Presentation. Case: Detailed investigation of Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd.'s Hooghly Data Park. Qualification: Top 6 Teams advance to Round 3 (Grand Finale). Key Areas of Investigation: Water consumption, groundwater stress and water-positive claims. Renewable energy commitments and net-zero targets. Employment claims and actual local job creation. Farmer partnerships and treated wastewater utilisation. Green certifications and environmental compliance. Financial, regulatory, reputational and social risks. From uncovering hidden organisational challenges through employee data to managing critical workplace decisions and navigating workforce disruptions, teams must demonstrate analytical thinking, strategic HR knowledge, leadership and adaptability. Assemble your team of four and experience the challenges of managing people, making decisions and shaping the future of work. details_text: KaalDrishti, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is a business analytics competition that challenges participants to step into the role of Data Investigators and uncover the truth behind a company's crisis. Teams of four will work with fragmented financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business information to identify hidden patterns, detect anomalies and establish the real cause of a problem. Across three challenging rounds, participants will investigate an unsolved business crisis, tackle analytical challenges and defend their conclusions through hypothesis testing and a live boardroom presentation. The event tests analytical thinking, data interpretation, statistical reasoning, problem-solving and the ability to convert data into meaningful business decisions. ROUND 1 – THE CRIME SCENE: FIND THE STORY Project Mirage – Uncover the Hidden Truth Participants will receive a business scenario, problem statement and relevant datasets. The case file will contain fragmented information such as financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business evidence. Teams must independently understand the situation, identify relevant patterns and anomalies, determine the root cause of the crisis and develop a hypothesis explaining what went wrong and why. Based on their analysis, teams must propose feasible business solutions while complying with the given constraints. Round Details: Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Open-Ended Data Investigation + Written Hypothesis Brief Submission: PDF deck of maximum 10 pages, excluding the Introduction and Closing slides. Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2. Evaluation Criteria: Understanding of the problem and root cause analysis. Analytical rigour specific to the dataset. Methodology adopted. Feasibility and quality of the proposed business solution. ROUND 2 – THE LOCKED DATA: UNLOCK THE EVIDENCE Xcelerate – Excel E-Sports The qualifying teams will enter an analytical challenge where they will be provided with a dataset and a problem statement. Participants must analyse the given information and develop an optimised solution or analytical model according to the requirements. Teams will be required to demonstrate their analytical capabilities using Microsoft Excel. They can use Excel charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins to develop and present their solutions. However, the final solution must be presented entirely in Excel. The methodology adopted and the plugins used must be explicitly mentioned. Submission/Presentation: The solution must be presented in Excel only. Qualification: Top 5 Teams advance to Round 3. Evaluation Focus: Analytical reasoning. Data interpretation and modelling. Problem-solving ability. Efficiency and accuracy of the solution. Methodology and effective use of Excel tools. ROUND 3 – THE FALSE TRAIL & THE BOARDROOM TRIAL: DELIVER THE VERDICT Find the Real Cause. Defend It Under Fire. Teams must test each hypothesis against the evidence collected in the earlier rounds, identify explanations based on bias, false correlation or manipulated data, and trace the crisis back to its Point of No Return — the exact past decision that set the crisis in motion. Participants will then present their final verdict and business recommendations before a jury acting as the company's Board, which will cross-examine their assumptions and conclusions. details_text: Overview YUGANTAR, presented by FINNOVATION as part of XAVIESTA 5.0, is an immersive marketing strategy competition that challenges participants to rewrite the destiny of a fictional Indian footwear brand. Through three interconnected rounds, teams will investigate the brand's history, uncover the strategic decision behind its downfall, rewrite a defining moment in its journey, and navigate the consequences of their choices. From analysing fragmented evidence and developing revised marketing strategies to tackling real-time marketing crises, participants must demonstrate their consumer understanding, analytical thinking, creativity and strategic decision-making. Here, every decision shapes the future, and every consequence tells a story. Round 1 – The Archive Decode the Brand Teams will receive a fragmented case archive containing old advertisements, consumer reviews, sales data, competitor movements, internal memos and market research relating to Kadam Footwear, a fictional Indian footwear brand. Participants must reconstruct the brand's timeline, identify the single strategic decision that changed its destiny and support their conclusions with evidence from the provided documents. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Fragmented Evidence Reconstruction + Written Hypothesis Brief Submission: One PDF containing: Reconstructed timeline of 8–12 events in chronological order. Hypothesis brief of maximum 500 words. Supporting evidence with document references. Qualification: Top 12 Teams Evaluation: Timeline accuracy, identification of the turning-point decision, evidence-based analysis and critical thinking. Round 2 – The Butterfly Effect Rewrite the Past The qualifying teams will get an opportunity to change one defining decision from Kadam Footwear's history. They must analyse how this single intervention could have altered the brand's journey, considering its impact on brand equity, market share, profit margins, competitive positioning and consumer perception. Based on their revised historical scenario, teams must develop a coherent marketing strategy and justify the consequences of their chosen intervention. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline Format: Single-Decision Rewrite + Revised Strategy Brief Challenge: Rewriting one historical decision and analysing its consequences. Submission: Revised strategy brief. Qualification: Top 6 Teams Evaluation: Strategic coherence, consequence analysis, marketing strategy, positioning and decision-making. Round 3 – The Present Break & Break the Chakra Survive 2027, Then Choose the Future The final round brings the consequences of each team's revised decision into the present. Each finalist will face a team-specific marketing crisis shaped by the changes introduced in Round 2. Teams must allocate a limited marketing budget across digital marketing, influencers, product, retail, partnerships and consumer research to respond to the crisis. They will then face a CEO-level dilemma, choosing whether to Accept, Alter or Reset the brand's future direction. The challenge concludes with a live boardroom presentation and jury cross-examination, where teams must defend their strategy and decisions. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline – Live Defence Format: Crisis Budget Allocation + CEO Dilemma + Jury Presentation & Cross-Examination Challenge: Team-specific marketing crisis and strategic decision-making. Finalists: Top 6 Teams from Round 2 Evaluation: Crisis management, resource allocation, consumer understanding, creativity, brand vision and strategic defence. Overall Rules & Regulations Each team must consist of exactly 4 members across all three rounds. No substitutions or changes in team composition will be permitted once registration is completed. details_text: Overview Step into the dynamic world of financial markets with ARTHCHAKRA, a flagship competition at XAVIESTA, presented by FINNOVATION – The Finance Club of Xavier Business School. Designed to test financial acumen, analytical thinking and strategic decision-making, the competition takes participants through three exciting stages: managing a virtual equity portfolio, crafting investment strategies tailored to real-world client objectives, and navigating unexpected market disruptions. With each round bringing a new challenge, participants must analyse, strategise, adapt and defend their investment decisions. Gather your team of four and embark on a journey where market knowledge meets strategic brilliance! Round 1 – Mock Stock Market Virtual Capital. Real Decisions. The first round is an online stock market simulation where teams receive virtual capital of ₹1,00,000 to build and manage an equity portfolio comprising NSE-listed stocks. Teams will be evaluated based on the final market value of their portfolios at the end of the designated trading period. The Top 15 performing teams will qualify for Round 2. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Virtual Capital: ₹1,00,000 per team Platform: National Stock Exchange (NSE) Investment: NSE-listed equity stocks only Maximum Stocks: 20 different stocks Format: Online Qualification: Top 15 Teams Round 2 – The Client Mandate Analyse. Allocate. Advise. Teams will receive a Client Investment Policy Statement (IPS) and a Market Assumptions Sheet. Based on the client's objectives and constraints, participants must construct a suitable investment portfolio while considering risk, return, liquidity and diversification. Teams must submit their portfolio allocation along with a written rationale explaining their investment decisions. The Top 10 teams will advance to the final round. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Format: Offline, Proctored Challenge: Client-Based Portfolio Construction Submission: Excel Portfolio, Written Rationale (250–350 words) and AI Usage Log Qualification: Top 10 Teams Round 3 – The Curveball Adapt. Rebalance. Defend. The final round introduces a sudden market shock along with a private client-specific twist. Teams must reassess their existing portfolios, evaluate the impact of changing market conditions and decide whether to retain or rebalance their investments. The round concludes with a live presentation and defence before a panel of judges, where teams must justify their investment strategies and decisions. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Format: Live Defence (Presentation & Q&A) Challenge: Market Shock and Client-Specific Twist Submission: Updated Excel Portfolio, Written Rationale (250–350 words) and AI Usage Log Evaluation: Strategic Decisions, Risk Assessment, Portfolio Rebalancing and Client Alignment Competition Details Institution: Xavier Business School, St. Xavier's University, Kolkata Team Size: 4 Members per Team Competition Structure: Round 1: Top 15 Teams Round 2: Top 10 Teams Round 3: Final Round – Winner Selection General Rules & Regulations Each team must consist of exactly 4 members . Cross-college teams are not permitted. The competition is open to college students . Participants must carry their valid College ID cards during offline rounds. No substitutions or changes in team composition will be permitted once registration is completed. The competition will consist of three rounds, with eliminations after Rounds 1 and 2. The top 15 teams from Round 1 will qualify for Round 2, and the top 10 teams from Round 2 will advance to the final round. Participants must maintain discipline and decorum throughout the competition. No communication, file-sharing or collaboration between competing teams is permitted during any round. Violations may lead to disqualification. The decisions of the judges and organising committee will be final and binding. The organising committee reserves the right to modify the rules, schedule or competition format if requir

details_text: About: Early-stage founders from across India compete in an online round, and the top teams pitch live to an investor panel at the offline grand finale on 7, 8 and 9 January 2027. Domains (choose one): Healthcare & HealthTech (finale day: 7 January 2027) Vertical B2B SaaS (finale day: 8 January 2027) B2B FinTech & Financial Infrastructure (finale day: 9 January 2027) Who Can Participate: Early-stage startups and founding teams from any city or college. Students, graduates and professionals are welcome. Teams of 1 to 5 members . Inter-college and inter-specialisation teams are allowed. One startup per team, registered in one domain. Startups must have an original idea, product or prototype in one of the three domains. Format: Round 1 (Online): Teams register and submit their startup details. The organising team evaluates and scores each entry. Selection: 25 finalist teams are chosen in each domain, 75 teams in total. Grand Finale (Offline): Finalists pitch live at AIKTC to an investor panel and domain experts on the day of their domain, take questions and receive feedback. Round timings, pitch duration and the detailed schedule will be shared with shortlisted teams. What Participants Get: A national stage and a live pitch in front of investors and domain experts Direct feedback from investors and experts The opportunity to pitch for investment of up to Rs 3 crore (an indicative ceiling, subject to investor decisions) Networking with founders, mentors and investors Visibility through the event's media and community partners Rules: Registration for the competition is free. All submissions must be original and accurate. Plagiarised or misleading information will lead to disqualification. Finalists must be able to attend the offline finale at AIKTC on their domain day. Participation does not guarantee funding. Investment decisions rest solely with investors, and any investment is agreed directly between the investor and the startup. Selected finalists will receive the finalist confirmation procedure and any applicable terms, including those relating to investor introductions, in writing from the organising team before they are asked to confirm their participation. The decisions of the organisers and judges are final. The schedule may be updated, and changes will be announced.

title: Perplexed: A Business Competition Powered by AI
organiser: Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology (TIET), Patiala
description: Date: 21st November Registration fees: 200 per participant Overview PERPLEXED is built around two partner companies whose businesses depend on each other, and both are struggling. Half the teams act as consulting firms…
details_text: Date: 21st November Registration fees: 200 per participant Overview PERPLEXED is built around two partner companies whose businesses depend on each other, and both are struggling. Half the teams act as consulting firms hired by Company A, and the other half are hired by Company B. The problems are real within the game, but are not given to teams directly. Teams discover them by interviewing AI chatbots playing company stakeholders, such as the CEO, CFO, operations head, HR manager or disgruntled employee. Each stakeholder knows only part of the story and may have their own agenda, hide or downplay facts, or misremember events. Teams must ask effective questions, connect clues, distinguish facts from spin, and present a clear diagnosis with practical recommendations to judges acting as the client's board. Not everything worth knowing is said out loud: the company portal also holds traces of everyday office life that may quietly support or contradict what stakeholders claim. Neither company's problems can be solved from inside one company: part of every root cause sits with the partner, and employees on each side may be quick to blame the other. Midway through the investigation, each team must find and convince a team working on the other company to form an alliance, combine what both sides know, and present a joint diagnosis. Eligibility: Open to students. Teams of 2-4. Performance Guidelines: Robots or simulated bots must follow arena rules and size limits. Online teams use the provided simulator; on-site teams must pass inspection. Robots may be modified between rounds. Judging Criteria Match results (50%) Strategy (20%) Robot performance (20%) Adaptation between rounds (10%).

description: Event Description: A high-speed, head-to-head robotics competition where custom-built robots face off in a 1v1 mechanical soccer match. Teams design, build, and pilot their manual bots in a purpose-built arena to…
details_text: Event Description: A high-speed, head-to-head robotics competition where custom-built robots face off in a 1v1 mechanical soccer match. Teams design, build, and pilot their manual bots in a purpose-built arena to outmaneuver opponents, defend their penalty zones, and score goals using a mini football. Date: 21st November (Tech Inspection & Pool Stage) / 22nd November (Knockouts & Finals) Registration Fee: ₹800- per Team Registration Process: Participants will have to register on the official Saturnalia registration platform before the deadline mentioned on the platform. Participation may be subject to shortlisting in case of an overwhelming response. Only shortlisted participants, if applicable, will be notified about the further process. Participants must provide the required details and complete all necessary registration formalities within the specified deadline. Participation is exclusively open to college students possessing valid college ID cards for the current academic year. Participants must carry their valid college ID card during the event. The registration fee, if applicable, will be communicated through the official registration platform. Rules & Regulations: Event Overview & Arena Specifications: Mayhem is the premier combat robotics tournament of Saturnalia. Engineering teams design and build wireless combat machines that can deliver active kinetic strikes while withstanding hostile impacts. A robot wins by disabling its opponent through a Technical Knockout (TKO), or by scoring the most points for Aggression, Control and Damage. Arena Specifications & Containment: Enclosure Footprint: 16 ft × 16 ft × 7 ft fully enclosed steel frame High-impact, shatter-resistant polycarbonate safety walls Reinforced perimeter base guards Active Floor Hazard Pit: A 3 ft × 3 ft automated floor pit opens during the final 60 seconds of every match round. Forcing an opposing robot completely into the pit is an instant TKO. Safety & Containment Systems: Dual hard-wired emergency arena kill switches Optical containment screens Active smoke and exhaust ventilation for battery safety Weight Classes, Roster & Eligibility: Every machine must pass formal technical inspection before competing. Weight limits are strictly enforced, with a maximum tolerance of 1%. Weight Classes: Featherweight: up to 8.0 kg (17.6 lbs) Middleweight: up to 15.0 kg (33.0 lbs) Heavyweight: up to 30.0 kg (66.0 lbs) Roster & Structural Rules: Team Roster: 2 to 6 registered members per team. Teams may include members from more than one college, provided everyone’s student credentials are verified. Dimensions: there is no limit on overall dimensions. The fully assembled robot must fit through the 4 ft × 4 ft arena access hatch without disassembly. Walker Bonus: robots using true non-wheeled linear walking mechanisms get an extra 10% weight allowance above their class limit. Cluster Bots: a team may deploy multiple sub-units under one entry. The combined mass and dimensions of all active sub-units must stay within the class limits. Technical, Power & Weapon Regulations: Control Systems & Radio: Radio Protocol: 2.4 GHz digital spread-spectrum systems with frequency-hopping channels. Prohibited Control: tethered remote connections and fully autonomous robots are strictly prohibited. Fail-Safe Requirement: all drive systems and weapon throttles must return to neutral/zero power immediately if the transmitter signal is lost or interrupted. Electrical Power & Battery Shielding: Voltage Cap: electric drive systems only. The potential between any two electrical points must not exceed 36 V DC. Engines: internal combustion engines (ICE) are banned. Battery Containment: every LiPo, LiFe or gel battery cell must be fully enclosed in a rigid enclosure of at least 2 mm steel or aluminium plate, to contain thermal runaway. Mobility & Weapons: Allowed Mobility: Wheels Treads Walking mechanisms Controlled hopping assemblies (maximum height clearance of 6 ft) Prohibited Mobility: Vacuu

Teams rebuild the brand in stages: first the logo and tagline, then the campaign, and finally the social media strategy. After every round, the judges score the work and the lowest-scoring teams are eliminated. Only the strongest five teams reach the final pitch, and the top three of them take the podium. title: HerHack
description: HERHACK 2026 is a 36-hour national-level hackathon for women innovators and developers to build solutions for real-world problems. The event will be held at the Echelon Institute of Technology in Faridabad, Haryana.
eligibility: Participants aged 18 and above, organized into teams of 2–5 members.
requirements: Original, track-relevant projects including a repository, documentation, and a project demonstration.
details_text: HERHACK 2026 — National Level Women-Focused Hackathon HERHACK 2026 is a 36-hour national-level hackathon organized at Echelon Institute of Technology, Faridabad, Haryana, bringing together women innovators, developers, students, and technology enthusiasts to build innovative solutions for real-world problems. EVENT DETAILS • Date: 20–21 November 2026 • Duration: 36 Hours • Venue: Echelon Institute of Technology, Faridabad, Haryana • Registration Fee: FREE • Team Size: 2–5 Members • Age Requirement: 18+ • Project Submission Deadline: 10 November 2026 TRACKS 1. Web3 / Blockchain Build innovative solutions using blockchain, decentralized technologies, smart contracts, digital assets, and Web3 infrastructure. 2. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Develop AI-powered solutions using machine learning, generative AI, computer vision, natural language processing, intelligent agents, or related technologies. 3. Internet of Things (IoT) Create connected solutions using sensors, embedded systems, smart devices, automation, and real-time data. 4. Student Innovation Build innovative technology solutions addressing real-world problems, campus challenges, social needs, or emerging opportunities. PRIZES Total Prize Pool: ₹2,00,000 Each of the four main tracks offers: 1st Prize — ₹20,000 2nd Prize — ₹15,000 3rd Prize — ₹10,000 Women Safety Special Winner — ₹20,000 The Women Safety Special Award is not a separate fifth track. A project addressing women safety can be submitted under any of the four official tracks and may additionally be considered for the special award. Goodies and certificates will also be provided to eligible participants as per the official event guidelines. SUBMISSION & HACKATHON Project Submission Deadline: 10 November 2026 HERHACK 2026 Hackathon: 20–21 November 2026 Participants must complete and submit their projects by the submission deadline. Selected teams will participate in the 36-hour hackathon and present their solutions for evaluation. ELIGIBILITY • Participants must be 18 years or above. • Teams must consist of 2–5 members. • Registration is completely free. • Participants must follow the official hackathon rules and submission requirements. PROJECT REQUIREMENTS • Projects must be original and relevant to the selected track. • Previously built projects should not be submitted as new hackathon projects. • Plagiarism or direct copying of existing projects is strictly prohibited. • Teams must provide the required project repository and documentation. • Teams should provide a project demonstration/video as required. • The final presentation should clearly communicate the problem, solution, technology, innovation, and impact. EVALUATION Projects will be evaluated based on: • Innovation • Technical Implementation • Problem Relevance • Real-World Impact • Usability • Scalability • Quality of Execution • Final Demonstration Detailed evaluation and submission instructions will be communicated to shortlisted participants. CERTIFICATES Participants will receive certificates as per the official event guidelines. JOIN THE HERHACK 2026 COMMUNITY Join the official HERHACK 2026 WhatsApp Community for important announcements, updates, coordination, and event-related communication. Join HERHACK 2026 WhatsApp Community OFFICIAL WEBSITE Visit the Official HERHACK 2026 Website Stay connected through the official website and WhatsApp Community for announcements, updates, submission instructions, shortlisting information, and other event-related communication.
